Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 11, verses 1–5:

Explanation of the words:

Alif-Lam-Ra: This is one of the disjoined letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'ah). It is written Alif-Lam-Ra and read Alif, Lam, Ra.

Uhkimat: That is, it was arranged in a sound order and composed in a manner free of any defect.

Fussilat: That is, through the clarification of rulings, stories, admonitions, and kinds of guidance.

Min ladun: That is, from the presence of the All-Wise, the All-Aware, who is Allah, glorified and exalted is He.

Mata'an hasanan: That is, with a good life and abundant provision.

Ila ajalin musamma: That is, the death of a person at the term decreed for him.

Wa yu'ti kulla dhi fadl: That is, and He will give every person of righteous and excellent deeds his excellent reward.

Adhab yawmin kabir: This is the punishment of the Day of Resurrection.

Yathnuna sudurahum: That is, they bow their heads over their chests so as to hide themselves from Allah, in their own supposition.

Yastaghshuna thiyabahum: They cover their heads and faces so that Allah will not see them, in their false view.

The meaning of the verses: His saying, the Exalted, ﴿Alif-Lam-Ra﴾: this letter is among the ambiguous (mutashabih) matters, and it is good to entrust its meaning to Allah, so it is said: Allah knows best what He intends by it. It conveys two benefits. The first: the noble Qur'an, with which Allah challenged them to produce its like or a surah like it, is composed of letters like these: Alif-Lam-Mim, Alif-Lam-Ra, Ta-Ha, Ta-Sin-Mim, Ha-Mim, Qaf, Nun. So they should produce its like, and if you are unable, know that it is the Book of Allah and His revelation, and that Muhammad is His servant and messenger, so believe in it. The second: since they did not want to hear the Qur'an, and were commanded to engage in idle talk during its recitation, and boasted of openly opposing it, these disjoined letters came in a way contrary to what they were accustomed to in their language and what they were used to in their Arabic dialects, compelling them to hear it. When they heard it, they were affected by it and believed. What an excellent benefit these disjoined letters conveyed.

His saying, the Exalted, ﴿A Book whose verses have been made precise﴾: That is, the book composed of these letters is a great book whose verses were arranged and organized in a sound order, free of any defect in their wording, their composition, or their meanings. His saying: ﴿Then detailed﴾: That is, it distinguishes what it contains of rulings and laws, admonitions, beliefs, manners, and morals, in a way that has no parallel in any book that came before. His saying: ﴿from One who is Wise and Acquainted﴾: That is, its detailing was undertaken by One who is Wise and Acquainted: Wise in His governance and disposition, Wise in His legislation, His nurturing, His judgment and decree, Acquainted with the circumstances of His servants and the affairs of His creation. Therefore His Book, His rulings, and His detailing are nothing but the highest example in all of that.

His saying: ﴿That you worship none but Allah. Indeed I am to you from Him a warner and a bringer of good tidings﴾: That is, the Book was sent down, its verses were made precise, and its rulings and kinds of guidance were detailed, so that you worship none but Allah, for there is no deity worthy of worship except Him, and no worship benefits except worship of Him. His saying: ﴿Indeed I am to you from Him a warner and a bringer of good tidings﴾: this is the statement of His messenger who conveys from Him, saying: O people, I am to you from Him, that is from your Lord, the Wise, the All-Knowing, a warner before a severe punishment if you do not repent, believe, and affirm His oneness. And a bringer of good tidings: that is, I give good news to whoever believes, affirms His oneness, and does righteous deeds, of Paradise in the Hereafter. ﴿And that you seek forgiveness of your Lord, then turn to Him in repentance, He will let you enjoy a good provision until a specified term﴾: That is, and that you seek forgiveness from your Lord by acknowledging your error in worshipping other than Him, then turn to Him, that is return to Him by believing in Him, His messenger, His promise and His threat, and obeying Him in His commands and prohibitions. In return you will have this: He will let you enjoy in this life a good provision with abundant blessings and many goods, until the end of your appointed terms, each one of you.

His saying: ﴿And He gives every person of virtue his virtue﴾: That is, He, glorified and exalted, will give every person of virtue in this world, of righteousness, charity, and goodness, his virtue on the Day of Resurrection, in the abode of honor, Paradise, the abode of the righteous. His saying: ﴿But if they turn away﴾: That is, if they turn away from this call and remain upon their polytheism and disbelief, ﴿indeed I fear for you the punishment of a great day﴾, which is the punishment of the Day of Resurrection. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿To Allah is your return﴾: after warning them of the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, He informs them that their return is to Him, the Exalted, without doubt; He will surely revive them after their death, gather them before Him, and recompense them by His justice and mercy. ﴿And He is Powerful over all things﴾: among that is their revival after death and their recompense, a bad deed with its like and a good deed with ten times its like. This is the justice and mercy for which there is no parallel.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Unquestionably, they fold their chests to hide from Him﴾: this kind of shameful and foolish conduct was practiced by some of them, who would bend their heads and incline them over their chests so that the Messenger ﷺ would not see them. Some did this supposing that they could conceal themselves from Allah, the Exalted, and this is the extreme of ignorance. Some did this out of hatred for the Messenger ﷺ, so that he would not see them. He, the Exalted, answered this with His saying: ﴿Unquestionably, when they cover themselves with their garments﴾: that is, they wrap themselves in them, ﴿He knows what they conceal and what they disclose. Indeed He is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾. So there is no sense in covering oneself with garments to hide from Allah, the Exalted, for Allah knows their secret and their open speech, and knows what their breasts conceal, even if they do this out of hatred for the Prophet ﷺ. Evil is what they have done, and He will recompense them for what they described; indeed He is Wise and Knowing.

Guidance from the verses:

1- A manifestation of the inimitability of the Qur'an: it is composed of disjoined letters, and the Arabs were unable to produce a surah like it.

2- Explanation of the reason for sending down the Book, the precision of its verses, and their detailing: that Allah alone be worshipped, and that the polytheists seek His forgiveness and then repent to Him, so that they may be perfected and prosper in this world and the Hereafter.

3- The obligation to abandon polytheism first, and then to devote worship sincerely second.

4- Good deeds are not lost before Allah when their doer is among the people of monotheism: ﴿And He gives every person of virtue his virtue﴾.

5- An explanation of the ignorance of the polytheists who hid from Allah with their heads and garments.

6- The return of people is to their Lord, whether they wish or not, and the recompense is just, and none is destroyed before Allah except one who is destined for destruction.

Wa yu'ti kulla dhi fadl: That is, and He will give every person of righteous and excellent deeds his excellent reward.

Adhab yawmin kabir: This is the punishment of the Day of Resurrection.

Yathnuna sudurahum: That is, they bow their heads over their chests so as to hide themselves from Allah, in their own supposition.

Yastaghshuna thiyabahum: They cover their heads and faces so that Allah will not see them, in their false view.

The meaning of the verses: His saying, the Exalted, ﴿Alif-Lam-Ra﴾: this letter is among the ambiguous (mutashabih) matters, and it is good to entrust its meaning to Allah, so it is said: Allah knows best what He intends by it. It conveys two benefits. The first: the noble Qur'an, with which Allah challenged them to produce its like or a surah like it, is composed of letters like these: Alif-Lam-Mim, Alif-Lam-Ra, Ta-Ha, Ta-Sin-Mim, Ha-Mim, Qaf, Nun. So they should produce its like, and if you are unable, know that it is the Book of Allah and His revelation, and that Muhammad is His servant and messenger, so believe in it. The second: since they did not want to hear the Qur'an, and were commanded to engage in idle talk during its recitation, and boasted of openly opposing it, these disjoined letters came in a way contrary to what they were accustomed to in their language and what they were used to in their Arabic dialects, compelling them to hear it. When they heard it, they were affected by it and believed. What an excellent benefit these disjoined letters conveyed.

His saying, the Exalted, ﴿A Book whose verses have been made precise﴾: That is, the book composed of these letters is a great book whose verses were arranged and organized in a sound order, free of any defect in their wording, their composition, or their meanings. His saying: ﴿Then detailed﴾: That is, it distinguishes what it contains of rulings and laws, admonitions, beliefs, manners, and morals, in a way that has no parallel in any book that came before. His saying: ﴿from One who is Wise and Acquainted﴾: That is, its detailing was undertaken by One who is Wise and Acquainted: Wise in His governance and disposition, Wise in His legislation, His nurturing, His judgment and decree, Acquainted with the circumstances of His servants and the affairs of His creation. Therefore His Book, His rulings, and His detailing are nothing but the highest example in all of that.

His saying: ﴿That you worship none but Allah. Indeed I am to you from Him a warner and a bringer of good tidings﴾: That is, the Book was sent down, its verses were made precise, and its rulings and kinds of guidance were detailed, so that you worship none but Allah, for there is no deity worthy of worship except Him, and no worship benefits except worship of Him. His saying: ﴿Indeed I am to you from Him a warner and a bringer of good tidings﴾: this is the statement of His messenger who conveys from Him, saying: O people, I am to you from Him, that is from your Lord, the Wise, the All-Knowing, a warner before a severe punishment if you do not repent, believe, and affirm His oneness. And a bringer of good tidings: that is, I give good news to whoever believes, affirms His oneness, and does righteous deeds, of Paradise in the Hereafter. ﴿And that you seek forgiveness of your Lord, then turn to Him in repentance, He will let you enjoy a good provision until a specified term﴾: That is, and that you seek forgiveness from your Lord by acknowledging your error in worshipping other than Him, then turn to Him, that is return to Him by believing in Him, His messenger, His promise and His threat, and obeying Him in His commands and prohibitions. In return you will have this: He will let you enjoy in this life a good provision with abundant blessings and many goods, until the end of your appointed terms, each one of you.

His saying: ﴿And He gives every person of virtue his virtue﴾: That is, He, glorified and exalted, will give every person of virtue in this world, of righteousness, charity, and goodness, his virtue on the Day of Resurrection, in the abode of honor, Paradise, the abode of the righteous. His saying: ﴿But if they turn away﴾: That is, if they turn away from this call and remain upon their polytheism and disbelief, ﴿indeed I fear for you the punishment of a great day﴾, which is the punishment of the Day of Resurrection. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿To Allah is your return﴾: after warning them of the punishment of the Day of Resurrection, He informs them that their return is to Him, the Exalted, without doubt; He will surely revive them after their death, gather them before Him, and recompense them by His justice and mercy. ﴿And He is Powerful over all things﴾: among that is their revival after death and their recompense, a bad deed with its like and a good deed with ten times its like. This is the justice and mercy for which there is no parallel.

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Unquestionably, they fold their chests to hide from Him﴾: this kind of shameful and foolish conduct was practiced by some of them, who would bend their heads and incline them over their chests so that the Messenger ﷺ would not see them. Some did this supposing that they could conceal themselves from Allah, the Exalted, and this is the extreme of ignorance. Some did this out of hatred for the Messenger ﷺ, so that he would not see them. He, the Exalted, answered this with His saying: ﴿Unquestionably, when they cover themselves with their garments﴾: that is, they wrap themselves in them, ﴿He knows what they conceal and what they disclose. Indeed He is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾. So there is no sense in covering oneself with garments to hide from Allah, the Exalted, for Allah knows their secret and their open speech, and knows what their breasts conceal, even if they do this out of hatred for the Prophet ﷺ. Evil is what they have done, and He will recompense them for what they described; indeed He is Wise and Knowing.

Guidance from the verses:

1- A manifestation of the inimitability of the Qur'an: it is composed of disjoined letters, and the Arabs were unable to produce a surah like it.

2- Explanation of the reason for sending down the Book, the precision of its verses, and their detailing: that Allah alone be worshipped, and that the polytheists seek His forgiveness and then repent to Him, so that they may be perfected and prosper in this world and the Hereafter.

3- The obligation to abandon polytheism first, and then to devote worship sincerely second.

4- Good deeds are not lost before Allah when their doer is among the people of monotheism: ﴿And He gives every person of virtue his virtue﴾.

5- An explanation of the ignorance of the polytheists who hid from Allah with their heads and garments.

6- The return of people is to their Lord, whether they wish or not, and the recompense is just, and none is destroyed before Allah except one who is destined for destruction.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 11, verse 6–8:

Explanation of the words:

*min dābbah* (every creature): any living thing that crawls on the earth, that walks, whether human or animal.

*mustaqarrahā* (its place of settlement): the place where it settles on the earth.

*wa-mustawdaʿahā* (its place of deposit): the place where it is deposited before it settles, such as the loins of men and the wombs of women.

*fī kitābin mubīn* (in a clear Book): that is, the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz).

*fī sittati ayyām* (in six days): that is, Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday.

*wa-kāna ʿarshuhu ʿalā al-māʾ* (and His Throne was upon the water): since He had not yet created any of the creatures other than it, and the water was upon the air.

*liyabluwakum* (that He may test you): that is, that He may try you, to see which of you is best in deed.

*ilā ummatin maʿdūdah* (for a limited period): that is, for a limited span of time.

*wa-ḥāqa bihim* (and there befell them): that is, descended upon them and encompassed them.

The meaning of the verses:

When Allah, the Exalted, informed in the previous verse that He is All-Knowing of what the breasts conceal, He mentioned in this verse manifestations of His knowledge and power, as confirmation of what the previous verse contained. So He, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And there is no creature on the earth⦆ — whether a human walking on the earth, or an animal that moves on it, crawling, walking on two legs or more, or flying in the sky — except that Allah has undertaken its provision, that is, by creating and bringing it into being, and by teaching it how to seek and obtain it. He, the Exalted, also knows its place of settlement on the earth, and likewise knows its place of deposit after its death, until it is resurrected on the Day of Resurrection.

His saying ﴿All of it is in a clear Book﴾ means that the creature, its provision, its place of settlement and its place of deposit have all been recorded before its creation in the Book of Decrees, the Preserved Tablet.

His saying in verse [7] ﴿And He it is who created the heavens and the earth in six days, and His Throne was upon the water﴾ means that He brought into being the seven heavens and the earth and what is in them within the span of six days. It is permissible that these be days like the days of this world, and permissible that they be like the days with Him, which are a thousand years, according to His saying in Surah al-Hajj: ﴿And indeed a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count﴾ [Verse 47]. His saying ﴿and His Throne was upon the water﴾ means that He created the Throne before the creation of the heavens and the earth. The Throne is the seat of sovereignty, and from it the governing of everything in this life is carried out. His saying ﴿upon the water﴾ — since there was neither earth nor heaven, there was nothing but water, like air. His saying ﴿that He may test you, which of you is best in deed﴾ means that He created you and created everything for your sake, that He may try you, to see which of you is most obedient to Him and best in deed, that is, in sincerity to Allah alone and in performing it in the manner that Allah legislated and His Messenger explained.

These are manifestations of His knowledge and power, the Exalted, and by them He alone deserves worship to the exclusion of anything else. By them it is known that nothing of the affairs of His servants is hidden from Him. So how do the ignorant attempt to conceal what is in their breasts and what their limbs do, by folding their breasts and covering their garments? Surely, evil is what they do.

His saying ﴿And if you say﴾ — O Messenger, to the polytheists — that you will be resurrected after death, that is, created anew and raised from your graves to be reckoned and recompensed according to your deeds in this worldly life, ﴿those who disbelieved will surely say﴾ — that is, upon hearing reports of the second life and what it contains of everlasting bliss and humiliating punishment — ﴿This is nothing but clear magic﴾ — that is, what Muhammad ﷺ says of this speech is nothing but clear magic, by which he intends to divert people from their pleasures and gather them around himself so that he may lead them and be served by them. It is false speech and a lying assumption, and this is the way of the disbeliever.

His saying in verse [8] ﴿And if We delay the punishment from them until a limited period﴾ means: and if We postpone, that is, defer, what We have threatened them with of punishment until limited times measured in hours, days, months and years, ﴿they will surely say, "What is holding it back?"﴾ — that is, what has restrained the punishment? They say this in denial and mockery. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Unquestionably, on the day it comes to them, it will not be turned away from them﴾ — that is, there is no one who can avert or repel it from them in any circumstance. ﴿And there will befall them what they used to ridicule﴾ — that is, the punishment they used to mock, by saying: "What is holding it back?!"

Guidance of the verses

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The vastness of Allah's knowledge and His undertaking of the provision of His creatures, human and animal.

2- Explanation of the creation of the universe and the purpose of creation.

3- Affirmation of the principle of the Final Resurrection after affirming the divinity of Allah, the Exalted.

4- One should not be deceived by Allah's granting respite to the people of disobedience, for He may seize them suddenly while they are unaware.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 11, verses 9–11:

Explanation of the words:

"Adhaqna al-insan" (We let man taste): i.e., We bestowed upon him mercy, that is, wealth and health.

"Thumma naza'naha minhu" (then We removed it from him): i.e., We stripped it from him.

"Ya'us kafur" (despairing, ungrateful): i.e., very much given to despair, that is, to hopelessness, and severely disbelieving.

"Na'ma'a ba'da darra'a" (blessing after hardship): i.e., good after evil.

"Al-sayyi'at" (the misfortunes): plural of sayyi'ah, which is that which afflicts one with hardship from calamities.

"Farih fakhur" (exultant, boastful): very much given to joy, happiness and exultation.

"Sabaru" (they were patient): i.e., in hardship and adversities.

"Maghfirah" (forgiveness): i.e., for their sins.

"Wa ajr kabir" (and a great reward): i.e., Paradise, the abode of the righteous.

Meaning of the verses:

He, exalted is He, informs that man who has not been illumined by the light of faith and has not adorned himself with righteous deeds, if Allah causes him to taste His mercy in the form of prosperity, ease of livelihood and bodily health, and then removes it from him for a matter that Allah wills, ﴿Indeed, he﴾, that is, that man, ﴿is despairing﴾, i.e., very much given to despair and hopelessness, ﴿ungrateful﴾ toward his Lord who bestowed favor upon him, denying what He had bestowed upon him.

As for His saying ﴿And if We let him taste blessing after hardship﴾, i.e., We let him taste the sweetness of blessing, the pleasure of ease, livelihood and bodily health after hardship that had befallen him from poverty and sickness, ﴿he will surely say﴾, instead of praising Allah and thanking Him for making him happy after misery, enriching him after poverty, and restoring his health after sickness, boastfully he says: ﴿The evils have gone away from me.﴾ ﴿Indeed, he is exultant﴾, i.e., very joyful, ﴿boastful﴾, i.e., very much given to pride and vainglory. The cause of this is the darkness of the soul due to disbelief and disobedience. As for the believing man who obeys Allah and His Messenger, it is the opposite: if he is granted ease he gives thanks, and if he is afflicted with hardship he is patient, because of the light of faith in his heart and the purification of his soul through good deeds.

This is what is contained in His, exalted is He, saying: ﴿Except those who are patient and do righteous deeds; those will have forgiveness﴾, i.e., for their sins, ﴿and a great reward﴾ from their Lord, which is Paradise, the abode of peace.

Lessons of the verses:

From the lessons of the verses:

1- That man, before he is purified by faith and righteous deeds, is in a state of extreme weakness and spiritual degradation.

2- Blame of despair and hopelessness, and their prohibition.

3- Blame of exultation in this world and boasting in it.

4- Clarification of the spiritual perfection of the believer, embodied in patience and gratitude, and clarification of his recompense with forgiveness and Paradise.

"Thumma naza'naha minhu" (then We removed it from him): i.e., We stripped it from him.

"Ya'us kafur" (despairing, ungrateful): i.e., very much given to despair, that is, to hopelessness, and severely disbelieving.

"Na'ma'a ba'da darra'a" (blessing after hardship): i.e., good after evil.

"Al-sayyi'at" (the misfortunes): plural of sayyi'ah, which is that which afflicts one with hardship from calamities.

"Farih fakhur" (exultant, boastful): very much given to joy, happiness and exultation.

"Sabaru" (they were patient): i.e., in hardship and adversities.

"Maghfirah" (forgiveness): i.e., for their sins.

"Wa ajr kabir" (and a great reward): i.e., Paradise, the abode of the righteous.

Meaning of the verses:

He, exalted is He, informs that man who has not been illumined by the light of faith and has not adorned himself with righteous deeds, if Allah causes him to taste His mercy in the form of prosperity, ease of livelihood and bodily health, and then removes it from him for a matter that Allah wills, ﴿Indeed, he﴾, that is, that man, ﴿is despairing﴾, i.e., very much given to despair and hopelessness, ﴿ungrateful﴾ toward his Lord who bestowed favor upon him, denying what He had bestowed upon him.

As for His saying ﴿And if We let him taste blessing after hardship﴾, i.e., We let him taste the sweetness of blessing, the pleasure of ease, livelihood and bodily health after hardship that had befallen him from poverty and sickness, ﴿he will surely say﴾, instead of praising Allah and thanking Him for making him happy after misery, enriching him after poverty, and restoring his health after sickness, boastfully he says: ﴿The evils have gone away from me.﴾ ﴿Indeed, he is exultant﴾, i.e., very joyful, ﴿boastful﴾, i.e., very much given to pride and vainglory. The cause of this is the darkness of the soul due to disbelief and disobedience. As for the believing man who obeys Allah and His Messenger, it is the opposite: if he is granted ease he gives thanks, and if he is afflicted with hardship he is patient, because of the light of faith in his heart and the purification of his soul through good deeds.

This is what is contained in His, exalted is He, saying: ﴿Except those who are patient and do righteous deeds; those will have forgiveness﴾, i.e., for their sins, ﴿and a great reward﴾ from their Lord, which is Paradise, the abode of peace.

Lessons of the verses:

From the lessons of the verses:

1- That man, before he is purified by faith and righteous deeds, is in a state of extreme weakness and spiritual degradation.

2- Blame of despair and hopelessness, and their prohibition.

3- Blame of exultation in this world and boasting in it.

4- Clarification of the spiritual perfection of the believer, embodied in patience and gratitude, and clarification of his recompense with forgiveness and Paradise.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 11, verses 12–14:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Fa-la'allaka﴾ (perhaps): an interrogative of denial, meaning that you should not abandon [any of it], and your chest should not be constricted.

Ḍā'iq bihi ṣadruka: constricted in your chest by its recitation to them, out of dislike that they would say such-and-such.

Kanz (treasure): abundant wealth from which one spends on oneself and on one's followers.

Wakīl: a watcher, a guardian.

Iftarāhu: he fabricated it and lied about it.

Man istaṭa'tum: whoever you are able to call upon to help you.

Fa-hal antum muslimūn: that is, submit to God, meaning yield to His command and surrender to Him.

The meaning of the verses:

After the polytheists repeatedly demanded of the Messenger ﷺ that he turn the mountains of Makkah into gold, among their proposals being: "Why has an angel not been sent down to him so that he may be a warner with him, or a treasure thrown down to him, or a garden for him to eat from," God the Exalted said to His Messenger ﷺ: ﴿Perhaps you would leave out part of what is revealed to you﴾, meaning, do not recite it to the polytheists nor convey it to them because of their indifference to it and their turning away from it. ﴿And your chest is constricted by it﴾, meaning by the Qur'an, out of dislike that you would confront them with it, and they would say ﴿"Why has a treasure not been sent down to him?"﴾, meaning abundant wealth on which he might live, which would indicate that God had sent him. ﴿Or an angel has not come with him﴾ to call to his call, confirm him in it, and bear witness to it. Such a thing should not be from you; that is, convey, and do not let your chest be constricted. ﴿You are only a warner﴾, meaning one who warns of the consequences of polytheism, disbelief, and sins. ﴿And God is Guardian over all things﴾, meaning the Watcher, the Guardian. As for you, nothing of that is upon you.

And His saying, ﴿Or do they say, "He has fabricated it"?﴾, meaning, rather, they say, "He has fabricated it," that is, he fabricated the Qur'an and said it from himself without it being revealed to him. Say, in refuting them: ﴿Then bring ten surahs like it, fabricated, and call upon whomever you are able to call, apart from God, to help you, if you are truthful﴾ in your claim that I fabricated it. If you cannot, and you will never be able to, then repent to your Lord and submit to Him.

And His saying, ﴿So if they do not respond to you﴾, meaning: say to them, O our Messenger, if those whom you have called upon do not respond to your support and you are unable, ﴿then know that it was sent down with the knowledge of God﴾, meaning the Qur'an was sent down accompanied by the knowledge of God, and that is the strongest proof that it is His revelation and His revealing. ﴿And that there is no god but He﴾, meaning that there is no god but God, and no worshipped one with right besides Him. Finally, ﴿So will you be Muslims?﴾, meaning: submit after the proof has been established against you through your inability, and that is better for you.

Guidance from the verses:

1- Clarification of God's guardianship over His Messenger, His granting him success, and His support for him.

2- Clarification of the obstinacy and arrogance in rejecting the truth shown by the polytheists.

3- Clarification that the Messenger ﷺ was not charged with guiding people; he was only charged with warning them of the consequences of their disbelief and disobedience, and after that, God the Exalted will requite them.

4- God the Exalted's challenge to the deniers of prophethood and monotheism to produce ten surahs like the Qur'an; they were unable, the proof was established against them, and it was confirmed that the Qur'an is the word and revelation of God, that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger, and that God—there is no god but He.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 11, verses 15–17:

Explanation of the words:

Zinat al-hayat al-dunya (the adornment of the worldly life): wealth, children, and kinds of clothing, food and drink.

Nuwaffi ilayhim: We give them the fruit of their deeds in full.

La yubkhasun: That is, their deeds' fruit is not diminished.

Wa habita (and became void): that is, it came to nothing and was corrupted.

Ala bayyinatin min rabbihi (upon a clear proof from their Lord): that is, upon certain knowledge.

Wa yatluhu shahidun minhu (and a witness from Him follows it): that is, it follows it.

Kitab Musa (the Book of Musa): that is, the Torah.

Wa man yakfur bihi (and whoever disbelieves in it): that is, in the Qur'an.

Fa-al-nar mawidhu (then the Fire is his promised place): that is, the place promised to him, to which he will certainly be brought down.

Fi miryatin minhu (in doubt about it): that is, in doubt concerning it.

The meaning of the verses:

When Allah the Exalted established the proof against the deniers by their inability to produce ten surahs like the Qur'an, fabricated, since they claimed that the Qur'an was fabricated and that Muhammad ﷺ had fabricated it, and nothing remained except that a person choose one of the two paths, the path of this world or the path of the Hereafter (Paradise or the Fire), Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment﴾ of wealth, children, rank, authority, luxurious clothing and fine furnishings.

﴿We shall pay them in full for their deeds therein﴾: We give them the fruit of their deeds in this world in full, without diminution. According to their effort and earnings in it they are given, and their deeds are not diminished for them, because of their disbelief and their abandonment. Then, after that, if they do not repent to their Lord, they die as disbelievers, having nothing but the Fire. ﴿And what they did therein is rendered void﴾ of the deeds in this abode, and what they used to do is nullified.

This is what the first verse [15] and the second [16] indicate, which is His saying: ﴿Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment, We pay them in full for their deeds therein, and they therein will not be defrauded. Those are the ones for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter but the Fire. And what they did therein becomes void, and worthless is what they used to do.﴾ And His saying in the third verse [17]: ﴿Is then one who is upon a clear proof from his Lord﴾ by what was revealed to him of the Qur'an, and what it contains of proofs and demonstrations of the Oneness of Allah, the prophethood of His Messenger, and the Hereafter. His saying ﴿and a witness from Him recites it﴾: that is, another proof follows that proof, namely the truthful tongue that speaks through it and its moral and spiritual perfections, such that when a Bedouin looked at him he said, "By Allah, this is not the face of a liar." A third proof is in His saying ﴿and before it was the Book of Musa﴾: that is, the Torah, ﴿as a guide and a mercy﴾, bearing witness to it, since it carried the descriptions of the Messenger and his attributes and the descriptions and attributes of his community at more than one place in it. Is then one who stands upon these clear signs, proofs and demonstrations of the soundness of his religion, like one who has no proof or demonstration but blind imitation of misguidance and of polytheists? His saying ﴿those believe in it﴾: that is, those for whom those clear signs, proofs and demonstrations are established, ﴿believe in it﴾: that is, in the true Qur'an, the true Prophet and the true religion. His saying: ﴿and whoever disbelieves in it﴾: that is, in the Qur'an, its Prophet and its religion, from among the factions, that is, from among all the sects, nations and peoples, ﴿then the Fire is his promised place﴾, and sufficient for him is Hell, and wretched is the destination.

His saying: ﴿So do not be in doubt about it﴾: that is, do not be in doubt concerning it, that is, concerning the fact that the promised place of whoever disbelieves in it from among the factions is the Fire.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, it is the truth from your Lord﴾: that is, the Qur'an, which the deniers denied, and what it contains of promise and warning, and the true religion; all of that is the established truth from your Lord, but ﴿most of the people do not believe﴾ even when the proofs appear, the signs shine forth and the demonstrations grow strong.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- Clarification of a reality: that disbelief does not prevent the disbeliever from producing, according to his effort, the gain of his hand; he reaps when he sows, profits when he trades, and produces when he manufactures.

2- Clarification that the disbeliever does not benefit from his deeds in this world, even if they are righteous, and that loss is inherent to him.

3- Muslims are upon a clear proof of their religion, while the followers of the other religions have no proof and are in the darkness of blind imitation and the misguidance of disbelief and ignorance.

5- Clarification of Allah's custom among people, which is that most of them do not believe.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 11, verses 18–20:

Explanation of the words:

*Wa man aẓlamu mimman iftarā ʿala Llāhi kadhiban* (And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against God): i.e., no one. The interrogative is for negation.

*Yuʿraḍūna ʿala rabbihim* (They will be presented before their Lord): i.e., on the Day of Resurrection.

*Al-ashhād* (the witnesses): plural of shāhid (witness). Here they are the angels.

*Laʿnatu Llāh* (the curse of God): i.e., His expulsion and distancing.

*ʿala al-ẓalimīn* (upon the wrongdoers): i.e., the polytheists.

*Sabīl Llāh* (the way of God): i.e., Islam.

*ʿiwajan* (crooked): i.e., crooked.

*Muʿjizīna fi al-arḍ* (able to escape in the earth): i.e., they cannot escape God, the Mighty and Majestic; rather He is able to seize them at any moment.

*Min awliyāʾ* (protectors): i.e., helpers who would shield them from the punishment of God.

*Wa mā kānū yubṣirūn* (and they could not see): this is due to their extreme aversion to the truth, so they are unable to hear it or see it.

Meaning of the verses:

After He established the fate of those who denied the Qur'an, and of the one to whom it was revealed, and of the laws it brought, God mentioned a kind of the crimes of the criminals for which they deserved the Fire, saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against God?﴾ i.e., there is no one among people more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against God, of any kind of lie, however small. And His words ﴿Those will be presented before their Lord﴾ i.e., those liars will be presented on the Day of Resurrection before their Lord, majestic is His majesty, on the plains of Resurrection. The witnesses among the angels will say, bearing witness against them: ﴿These are the ones who lied against their Lord.﴾ Then a herald will proclaim: ﴿Unquestionably, the curse of God is upon the wrongdoers﴾ i.e., unquestionably, there is distance for them from Paradise and expulsion from it into the Fire of Hell.

Then God clarified the nature of their offenses for which they deserved the Fire, saying: ﴿who turn away from the way of God﴾ i.e., they turn themselves and others away from the Islamic religion, ﴿and seek to make it crooked﴾ i.e., they want the way of God to be crooked as they desire and crave. Lessons from the verses:

1- The gravity of the sin of one who lies against God, the Exalted, by attributing a son or a partner to Him, or by speaking about Him without knowledge.

2- The gravity of the crime of one who turns people away from Islam by his tongue, his state, or his authority.

3- The gravity of the sin of one who seeks to bend the Islamic law to his desires and appetites through false interpretations and irresponsible fatwas from those who have sold their Hereafter for their worldly life.

4- Clarification that one who hates a saying or a person cannot bear to see or hear it.

**Explanation of the Words:**

*"And what they used to fabricate will have vanished from them"*: That is, what they used to claim as partners to Allah, the Exalted, will have disappeared from them.

*"Undoubtedly"* (lā jarama): That is, truly and certainly, that in the Hereafter they are the greatest losers.

*"And they humbled themselves to their Lord"* (wa akhbatū ilā rabbihim): That is, they submitted or became humble before their Lord, through obedience to Him and fear of Him.

*"The likeness of the two groups"* (mathal al-farīqayn): That is, the group of the believers and the group of the disbelievers.

*"Will you not then be mindful?"* (afalā tadhakkarūn): That is, will you not take heed, so that you seek forgiveness from your Lord and then turn in repentance to Him?

**The Meaning of the Verses:**

The context continues to define the criminals and describe their state in the Hereafter. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Those are the ones who have lost their souls⦆ — that is, the far-removed — ﴿who have lost themselves⦆, for they have settled in the abode of misery and so have lost everything, even themselves. ﴿And what they used to fabricate will have vanished from them⦆ — that is, what they used to claim, that they had partners who would intercede for them and help them, will have disappeared. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Undoubtedly⦆ — that is, truly — ﴿that they, in the Hereafter⦆ — that is, in the abode of the Hereafter — ﴿they are the greatest losers⦆ — that is, the most losing of all others, because they added to the crime of their disbelief the crime of causing others to disbelieve, those whom they used to call to misguidance and turn away from Islam, the path of guidance and salvation from the Fire.

Having mentioned the state of the disbelievers and the loss they have come to, Allah, the Exalted, then mentions the state of the believers, saying: ﴿Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds⦆ — that is, who believed in Allah and in His promise and His threat, and believed in the Messenger of Allah and in what he brought, and did the righteous deeds which Allah, the Exalted, prescribed for them, such as prayer and zakah — ﴿and humbled themselves to their Lord⦆ — that is, they submitted their faces and hearts to Him, and yielded to Him with their limbs, humbling and submitting themselves — ﴿those are the companions of Paradise⦆, that is, its people — ﴿they will abide therein eternally⦆ — that is, they will not depart from it nor be transferred from it.

This is what the three verses indicate. As for the fourth verse [24], which is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿The example of the two groups is like the blind and the deaf and the seeing and the hearing. Are they equal in comparison?⦆ — Allah, the Exalted, has mentioned a comparison between the people of polytheism and the people of monotheism, to clarify the meaning and affirm the ruling. He says: ﴿The example of the two groups⦆ — that is, the description clarifying the two is like the blind and the deaf, and this is the group of disbelief and wrongdoing; and the seeing and the hearing, and this is the group of faith and monotheism. ﴿Are they equal in comparison?⦆ — that is, the answer to the description is no, because there is a difference between the blind and the seeing just as there is a difference between the deaf and the hearing. Which sensible person would consent to have blindness and deafness as his attributes and not have sight and hearing as his attributes? The answer is then: no one. ﴿Will you not then be mindful?⦆ — that is, will you not take heed from this example and turn in repentance to your Lord, so that you believe in Him, affirm His oneness, believe in His Messenger and follow him, and in His Book and act upon what is in it?

**Guidance from the Verses:**

1. The commendability of comparisons between opposites, for the sake of lesson and admonition.
2. The disbeliever is dead in a spiritual sense, therefore he neither hears nor sees; the Muslim is alive, therefore he is hearing and seeing.
3. The clarification of the inheritors of the abode of bliss, who are the people of faith and obedience, and the inheritors of the abode of loss, who are the people of disbelief and wrongdoing.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 11, Verses 25–27**

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 11, verses 28–31**

**Explanation of the words:**

*Ara'aytum* (أرأيتم): that is, tell me.

*'Ala bayyinatin min Rabbi* (على بينة من ربي): that is, upon knowledge that Allah taught me, so I knew that there is no god but Allah.

*Fa'ummiyat 'alaykum* (فعميت عليكم): that is, it was hidden from you, so you did not see it.

*Anulzimukumuha* (أنُلزِمُكمُوها): that is, compel you to accept it.

*Bi-taridi alladhina amanu* (بطارد الذين آمنوا): that is, by driving away from me those around me.

*Khaza'in Allah* (خزائن الله): those which contain bounty and wealth.

*Tazdari a'yunukum* (تزدري أعينكم): will look down upon your eyes, that is, will despise them.

**The meaning of the verses:**

The context remains the story of Noah with his people. Allah, the Exalted, informs that Noah said to his people, "Ara'aytum," that is, tell me, "if I am upon a clear proof from my Lord," that is, upon certain knowledge of Him, the Exalted, and of His attributes, and of what He commanded me regarding His worship, His Oneness, and calling to that. And His saying, ﴿and has given me mercy from Himself﴾, refers to revelation, prophethood, and success in worshipping Him. ﴿But it has been concealed from you﴾, that is, you have not seen it. ﴿So what can I do? Shall we compel you to accept it﴾, that is, shall I and those who believe with me compel you to see it, believe in it, and act by its guidance, ﴿while you are averse to it﴾, that is, while you are in the state of being averse to it. One who is averse to a thing scarcely sees it or hears it. This is what the first verse [27] indicates.

As for the second verse, Allah, the Exalted, also reports what Noah said to his people: ﴿And O my people, I do not ask you for wealth in return for it﴾, that is, I do not ask you for a wage in return for conveying to you this mercy which has been concealed from you so that you do not see it. ﴿My reward is only from Allah﴾, that is, my reward is only from Allah, for it is He who charged me with acting upon it and calling to it, and promised me a reward for it. And His saying, ﴿Nor am I one to drive away the believers﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 114], that is, I will not obey you in driving away the believers around me as you have proposed to me. ﴿Indeed, they will meet their Lord,﴾ and He will hold them to account and recompense them for their deeds. So how could it be proper for me to keep them away from hearing the truth, learning it, and taking hold of it, so that they may be perfected and be happy? For the measure is the purification of souls and the cleansing of spirits through faith and righteous deeds, not through nobility, wealth, and status as you imagine. Therefore, ﴿I see you as a people who are ignorant.﴾ This is what the second verse [28] indicates.

Then He said to them in the third verse, ﴿And O my people, who would help me against Allah if I drove them away?﴾ That is, who is it that would repel from me the punishment of Allah and protect me from it if I disobeyed Him by driving away, that is, by removing and distancing, the worshippers who believe from hearing guidance and learning goodness? There is no cause for that except that they are poor and weak, and ﴿your eyes look down upon them﴾, the sick eyes that are unable to see the truth, its people, and those who call to it. Then he said to them, ﴿Will you not then be mindful?﴾ That is, will you not reflect, so that you know your error and ignorance and return to right guidance, and repent to your Lord, so that you believe in Him and His Messenger, and worship Him alone with no partner. Then he said to them in the final verse [31], ﴿And I do not say to you that I possess the treasures of Allah,﴾ in response to their saying, ﴿We see no superiority in you over us﴾ [Hud: 27]. ﴿Nor do I know the unseen,﴾ so that I would know what is hidden in people's hearts and drive away this one and keep that one. ﴿Nor do I say that I am an angel,﴾ so that you would say, "We see you only as a human like us." ﴿Nor do I say of those whom your eyes look down upon,﴾ because of their poverty and weakness, ﴿that Allah will never grant them any good. Allah knows best what is within their souls,﴾ that is, whether sincerity or hypocrisy, and whether love for me or hatred. It is as if they had slandered the believers and accused them of hypocrisy, or that they had corrupt aims or material desires for which they gathered around Noah. And His saying, ﴿Indeed, then I would be among the wrongdoers,﴾ that is, if I said to the weak believers that Allah will never grant you any good, I would thereafter be among the wrongdoers who transgress against people by wronging them in their rights and degrading their dignity.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1) Aversion to a thing makes its possessor unable to see it, hear it, or understand what is said about it.

2) Disapproval of taking wages for calling to religion, for upbringing, and for religious teaching.

3) The obligation to respect and honour the weak, and the prohibition of despising and looking down upon them.

4) Knowledge of the unseen is exclusive to Allah, the Exalted, apart from all His creation, except for whomever Allah has taught some of it, for he then knows it.

5) The prohibition of belittling people, despising them, and mocking them.

And His saying, ﴿Nor am I one to drive away the believers﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara': 114], that is, I will not obey you in driving away the believers around me as you have proposed to me. ﴿Indeed, they will meet their Lord,﴾ and He will hold them to account and recompense them for their deeds. So how could it be proper for me to keep them away from hearing the truth, learning it, and taking hold of it, so that they may be perfected and be happy? For the measure is the purification of souls and the cleansing of spirits through faith and righteous deeds, not through nobility, wealth, and status as you imagine. Therefore, ﴿I see you as a people who are ignorant.﴾ This is what the second verse [28] indicates.

Then He said to them in the third verse, ﴿And O my people, who would help me against Allah if I drove them away?﴾ That is, who is it that would repel from me the punishment of Allah and protect me from it if I disobeyed Him by driving away, that is, by removing and distancing, the worshippers who believe from hearing guidance and learning goodness? There is no cause for that except that they are poor and weak, and ﴿your eyes look down upon them﴾, the sick eyes that are unable to see the truth, its people, and those who call to it. Then he said to them, ﴿Will you not then be mindful?﴾ That is, will you not reflect, so that you know your error and ignorance and return to right guidance, and repent to your Lord, so that you believe in Him and His Messenger, and worship Him alone with no partner. Then he said to them in the final verse [31], ﴿And I do not say to you that I possess the treasures of Allah,﴾ in response to their saying, ﴿We see no superiority in you over us﴾ [Hud: 27]. ﴿Nor do I know the unseen,﴾ so that I would know what is hidden in people's hearts and drive away this one and keep that one. ﴿Nor do I say that I am an angel,﴾ so that you would say, "We see you only as a human like us." ﴿Nor do I say of those whom your eyes look down upon,﴾ because of their poverty and weakness, ﴿that Allah will never grant them any good. Allah knows best what is within their souls,﴾ that is, whether sincerity or hypocrisy, and whether love for me or hatred. It is as if they had slandered the believers and accused them of hypocrisy, or that they had corrupt aims or material desires for which they gathered around Noah. And His saying, ﴿Indeed, then I would be among the wrongdoers,﴾ that is, if I said to the weak believers that Allah will never grant you any good, I would thereafter be among the wrongdoers who transgress against people by wronging them in their rights and degrading their dignity.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1) Aversion to a thing makes its possessor unable to see it, hear it, or understand what is said about it.

2) Disapproval of taking wages for calling to religion, for upbringing, and for religious teaching.

3) The obligation to respect and honour the weak, and the prohibition of despising and looking down upon them.

4) Knowledge of the unseen is exclusive to Allah, the Exalted, apart from all His creation, except for whomever Allah has taught some of it, for he then knows it.

5) The prohibition of belittling people, despising them, and mocking them.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 11, verses 32–34:

Explanation of the words:

Jadaltana (you have disputed with us): i.e., you have argued against us, wanting to cast us down and to deny us standing in our religion and in what we follow.

Bima ta'idna (what you promise us): i.e., the punishment, if we do not believe in what you call us to.

In kunta min al-sadiqin (if you are among the truthful): i.e., in your claim to prophethood and in reporting from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Bi-mu'jizin (able to escape): i.e., overcoming Allah, or escaping Him, whenever Allah wills to punish you.

Nushi (my counsel): i.e., my warning you of the punishment of your Lord if you remain in disbelief in Him, in meeting Him, and in His Messenger.

An yughwiyakum (that He lead you astray): i.e., that He cast you into error and keep you in it, so that He never guides you.

Meaning of the verses:

The context continues with the story of Nuh (peace be upon him) and his people. Allah, the Exalted, reports the words of the people of Nuh to him: He said, ﴿They said: O Nuh, you have disputed with us and multiplied your disputation, so bring us what you promise us, if you are among the truthful﴾, i.e., you have argued with us and multiplied your argument; so hasten the punishment and send it down upon us, if you are among the truthful in what you say, call to, and promise. Allah, the Exalted, then reports Nuh's response to their saying, which is what his Lord had taught him: He said, ﴿Only Allah will bring it to you, if He wills, and you will not escape﴾, i.e., you will not overcome Allah, nor flee from Him. And his saying: ﴿My counsel will not benefit you, even if I wished to advise you, if Allah intends to lead you astray. He is your Lord, and to Him you will be returned﴾. That is, my counsel will not benefit you, meaning you will not accept it no matter how much I wish it and exert myself in it, if Allah, Majestic is His majesty, intends to lead you astray because of what has preceded from you, and because of your obstinacy, disbelief, denial, and arrogance. For such people do not deserve Allah's guidance; rather, error is more fitting for them, until they perish in error and are wretched in the Hereafter. And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿He is your Lord, and to Him you will be returned﴾, i.e., the matter belongs to Him. Are you not His servants and He your Lord? If He wills, He will have mercy on you, and if He wills, He will punish you, though His wisdom negates that He punish the righteous and show mercy to the deviant wrongdoers.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The legitimacy of disputation to establish the truth and refute falsehood, on condition of good manner.

2- Allah's will precedes every will: what Allah wills occurs, and what He does not will does not occur.

3- The counsel of advisers does not benefit unless Allah wills good for the one advised.

4- One should not pass judgment on a servant who has not died, for his final state is known only at death, except by saying "Allah knows best."

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 11, verse 35:

Explanation of the words:

"Am yaqooloona" (Or do they say): that is, "Rather, do they say..."

"Iftarahu" (He has invented it): that is, he fabricated it and said it on his own, and it was not revealed to him.

"Fa-'alayya ijrami" (Then upon me is my crime): that is, the consequence of the lie, which is the crime, falls upon me and not upon anyone else.

"Wa ana bari'" (And I am innocent): that is, I disown and disassociate myself from your crime, so I do not bear its responsibility.

"Mimma tujrimoon" (From what you commit as crime): that is, against your own selves, by corrupting them with polytheism, disbelief and disobedience.

The meaning of the verse:

This noble verse was placed by its Revealer, glorified and exalted is He, between sections of the narrative about Noah and his people. Its placement here is apt, because narrating the story of Noah and his people is not possible for anyone except a prophet to whom revelation is sent, given how distant that history is. The Prophet's recounting of it today is therefore evidence that he is a prophet to whom revelation is sent. Hence He said, "Am yaqooloona iftarahu" (Or do they say, "He has invented it"?), meaning: they say the Qur'an was invented and fabricated, and that it was not revealed to him. "Qul in iftaytuhu fa-'alayya ijrami" (Say: If I have invented it, as you claim, then upon me is the burden of my lie), meaning: the sin of my lie is mine. "Wa ana bari'un mimma tujrimoon" (And I am innocent of what you commit as crime), meaning: you are responsible for your denial of me and your disbelief in your Lord, His Messenger, His promise and His warning.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- It is permissible to interject within speech when the placement is fitting, to establish a proof, to refute falsehood, or to draw attention to an important matter.

2- Relating stories is the greatest evidence of the truthfulness of the Prophet ﷺ in his claim to prophethood and of his call to God, the Exalted.

3- Establishing the principle that every person bears responsibility for their own deeds, and that no bearer of burdens shall bear the burden of another.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 11, verses 36–39:

Explanation of the words:

Wa-awha ila Nuh (And it was revealed to Nuh): i.e., he was informed by way of wahy (revelation), which is swift, hidden notification.

Fa-la tabta's (So do not grieve): do not be sad, and do not let grief overwhelm you, for I will save you and destroy them.

Al-fulk (the ship): i.e., the ship We commanded you to build to carry the believers upon it.

Sakhiru minhu (they mocked him): i.e., they ridiculed him, as in their saying: "You carry this ship to the sea," or "You carry the sea to it."

Yukhzihi (will disgrace him): i.e., will humiliate him and debase him.

Wa-yahillu alayhi adhab muqim (and upon him will descend a lasting punishment): i.e., the punishment of the Fire will befall him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will not be parted from it.

Meaning of the verses:

After the parenthetical statement in verse [35], the discourse returns to the account of Nuh and his people, and Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And it was revealed to Nuh that none of your people will believe, except those who have already believed﴾. This was after a call that lasted about nine hundred and fifty years; that is, from this day on, none of your people will believe. Therefore, ﴿do not grieve﴾, i.e., do not be distressed or saddened by what they do of evil, corruption, disbelief and sins, for I will save you and those believers with you, and destroy them by drowning. As for the Exalted's saying in the second verse [37]: ﴿And build the ship under Our eyes and by Our revelation﴾, i.e., We commanded him to build the ship, meaning the vessel, under Our watch, by Our direction and Our instruction, since he did not know ships or how to build them. And His saying ﴿and do not address Me concerning those who have wronged﴾, i.e., do not ask Me to avert the punishment from them or intercede for them to lighten it, for We have decreed their destruction by the flood, so they are certainly to be drowned. The Exalted's saying: ﴿And he was building the ship, and whenever a company of his people passed by him, they mocked him﴾. Allah the Exalted informs of Nuh's condition as he builds the ship, cutting the wood, planing it and assembling it, while his people pass by him; and whenever the nobles and leaders of the people passed by him, they mocked him, saying, "O Nuh, you have become a carpenter," or "Will you carry the sea to it, or carry it to the sea?" Then Nuh, peace be upon him, responded with His saying: ﴿If you mock us, then we will mock you as you mock﴾, i.e., us. ﴿So you will come to know﴾, i.e., in the future, who will receive a punishment that disgraces him, i.e., humiliates him and breaks the pride of his arrogance, and upon whom will descend a lasting punishment, which is the punishment of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection, a constant punishment that never ends.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Disapproval of grief, sorrow and regret over what the people of falsehood, evil and corruption do.

2- Explanation of the history of ship-building, and that it was by Allah's teaching to Nuh, peace be upon him.

3- Explanation of the human custom of mocking and ridiculing the people of truth and their callers, due to the darkness of their souls through disbelief and sins.

4- Demonstration of the truthfulness of Allah's promise to His messengers.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 11, verses 40–44:

Explanation of the words:

Fara al-tannur (فار التنور): the water gushed out and rose up from the tannur, the place where bread is baked.

Zawjayn ithnayn (زوجين اثنين): a pair of two, i.e. of every male and female among all the various kinds of creatures.

Wa-ahlaka (وأهلك): i.e. your wife and your children.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 11, verses 45–49:

Explanation of the words:

"من أهلي" (min ahli): i.e., among my family, including wives and children.

"وإن وعدك الحق" (wa inna wa'daka al-haqq): i.e., the promise that is firm and never fails.

"إنه عمل غير صالح" (innahu 'amalun ghayru salih): i.e., your asking me this is an unrighteous deed.

"أعظك" (a'idhuka): i.e., I forbid you and warn you lest you be among the ignorant.

"من الجاهلين" (min al-jahilin): i.e., among those who do not know My majesty, the truthfulness of My promise, and My faithfulness, so that you ask Me about what you have no knowledge of.

"سنمتعهم" (sanumatti'uhum): i.e., We will provide them with sustenance and enjoyments until the end of their terms, and then My punishment will befall them, and they are the disbelievers.

"للمتقين" (lilmuttaqin): i.e., those who fear Allah, worship Him, and do not associate anything with Him.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to speak of Noah and his people. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And Noah called out to his Lord⌉ i.e., he called upon Him, asking, ﴿"My Lord, indeed my son is of my family, and indeed Your promise is true, and You are the most just of judges."﴾ This was said by him at the time of boarding the ark, when his son Kan'an refused to board. That is: "My Lord, my son Kan'an is from my wife and among my children, and You promised that You would save me, my family, and those who are with me of the believers." ﴿And indeed Your promise is true﴾, i.e., the one that never fails at all. ﴿And You are the most just of judges﴾, i.e., the most knowing and most just of them. "This son of mine has disobeyed me, did not board with me, and will perish with the perishers unless You have mercy on him, O Lord of the worlds." Then the Lord, blessed and exalted, answered him with His true word: ﴿"Indeed, he is not of your family"﴾, i.e., those whom I promised to save, because he is not of your religion and not on your path. ﴿"Indeed, he is an unrighteous deed"﴾, i.e., your asking Me this, to save your son who is a disbeliever not of your creed, is an unrighteous deed. I had already informed you that I would drown the disbelievers. This request of yours is an unrighteous deed issuing from you. ﴿"I admonish you"﴾, i.e., I forbid you and warn you ﴿"lest you be among the ignorant"﴾, so that you ask Me about what you have no knowledge of. Noah said: ﴿"My Lord"﴾, i.e., "O my Lord, I seek refuge in You", meaning I seek protection and take shelter in You from asking You again about what I have no knowledge of. ﴿"And unless You forgive me and have mercy on me, I will be among the losers"﴾, i.e., those who have cheated themselves of their portions and so perished. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 11, verses 50–52:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And to ʿĀd, their brother Hūd.﴾ That is: We sent to the tribe of ʿĀd their brother Hūd, a brother to them in lineage, not in religion. Hūd was from the tribe of ʿĀd, and ʿĀd was a descendant of Sām ibn Nūḥ (peace be upon him).

﴿Worship Allah.﴾ That is: worship Him alone, and do not associate with Him any other.

﴿You have no god other than Him.﴾ That is: you have no deity worthy of your worship besides Him.

﴿You are but fabricators.﴾ That is: in making gods of other than Allah, from idols, you are nothing but liars.

﴿I do not ask you for any payment for it.﴾ That is: I do not seek from you any wage for conveying the call to monotheism to you.

﴿He who created me (faṭaranī).﴾ That is: who created me.

﴿Abundant rain (midrāran).﴾ That is: one from which the falling rain pours down abundantly.

﴿And do not turn away as criminals.﴾ That is: do not turn away from the call to monotheism as wrongdoers against your own souls by associating partners with Allah.

Meaning of the verses:

Here begins the account of Hūd with his people ʿĀd, after the account of Nūḥ (peace be upon him), and the purpose of the account is to establish the Oneness of Allah and the prophethood of the Messenger Muḥammad (ﷺ). Allah says, ﴿And to ʿĀd, their brother Hūd﴾, that is: We sent to the tribe of ʿĀd their brother Hūd, who was their brother in lineage and the first to speak Arabic. He is one of four prophets from among the Arabs: Hūd, Ṣāliḥ, Shuʿayb, and Muḥammad (ﷺ). His saying, ﴿O my people, worship Allah﴾, means: Hūd said to his people, after Allah had sent him to them, "O my people, worship Allah," that is, make Him One in worship, so do not worship anything alongside Him, for you have no god other than Allah, the Glorified and Exalted. His saying, ﴿You are but fabricators﴾, means: in your worship of other than Allah, of idols and images, you are nothing but liars, since your Lord Allah did not command you to worship them, and you have only lied against Him in this. His saying, ﴿O my people, I do not ask you for any payment for it﴾, means: I do not ask you for anything for my calling you to the Oneness of your Lord, so that you may complete your worship of Him and attain happiness; payment means wealth. ﴿My reward is only from He who created me﴾, that is: my reward is only from Allah, who created me. His saying, ﴿Will you not reason?﴾, means: will you not reason that if I were seeking a reward for my call to monotheism, I would have asked it of you? But I have not sought any reward from anyone other than my Lord, and thereby my sincerity in calling you and my counsel to you has become manifest.

As for Allah's statement, quoting the words of Hūd, ﴿And O my people, seek forgiveness from your Lord, then turn to Him in repentance﴾, Allah informs that Hūd called out to his people and said, "O my people, seek forgiveness from your Lord," that is, believe in Him and ask Him for forgiveness of your sins; "then repent to Him," that is, return to worshipping Him alone in the manner He has prescribed for you through your Prophet, and leave the worship of anything else. He will reward you by sending the sky upon you ﴿in abundant rain﴾, that is, with successive downpours, after the drought, famine and barrenness that had struck you, and He will add to your strength, a spiritual strength added to your material strength. His saying, ﴿And do not turn away as criminals﴾, is a warning, counselling them not to reject his advice and return to worshipping idols, for then they would be criminals against themselves, corrupting themselves with the filth of association and disobedience.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The call of the Messengers, from Nūḥ to Muḥammad (ﷺ), is one and the same: that Allah alone be worshipped.

2- Establishing the principle of "There is no god but Allah" (lā ilāha illā Allāh).

3- Polytheists and innovators are all fabricators against Allah and liars, since they worship Him in ways He has not prescribed for them.

4- The obligation of sincerity in calling to the faith.

5- The virtue of seeking forgiveness and the obligation of repentance.

6- Placing seeking forgiveness before repentance indicates that if a servant does not first acknowledge his sin, he cannot repent from it.

﴿I do not ask you for any payment for it.﴾ That is: I do not seek from you any wage for conveying the call to monotheism to you.

﴿He who created me (faṭaranī).﴾ That is: who created me.

﴿Abundant rain (midrāran).﴾ That is: one from which the falling rain pours down abundantly.

Meaning of the verses:

Here begins the account of Hūd with his people ʿĀd, after the account of Nūḥ (peace be upon him), and the purpose of the account is to establish the Oneness of Allah and the prophethood of the Messenger Muḥammad (ﷺ). Allah says, ﴿And to ʿĀd, their brother Hūd﴾, that is: We sent to the tribe of ʿĀd their brother Hūd, who was their brother in lineage and the first to speak Arabic. His saying, ﴿O my people, worship Allah﴾, means: Hūd said to his people, after Allah had sent him to them, "O my people, worship Allah," that is, make Him One in worship, so do not worship anything alongside Him, for you have no god other than Allah, the Glorified and Exalted. His saying, ﴿You are but fabricators﴾, means: in your worship of other than Allah, of idols and images, you are nothing but liars, since your Lord Allah did not command you to worship them, and you have only lied against Him in this. But I have not sought any reward from anyone other than my Lord, and thereby my sincerity in calling you and my counsel to you has become manifest.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 11, verses 53–57:

Explanation of the words:

Bayyinah (clear proof): that is, with a proof and evidence for the truth of what you call us to, namely the worship of God alone.

"Wa ma nahnu bi-tarikī ālihatinā" (We will not abandon our gods): that is, abandoning the worship of our gods because of your saying that they do not deserve to be worshipped.

"Illā i'tarāka" (except that it has struck you): that is, it has afflicted you.

Bi-sū' (with harm): that is, with derangement, for you are raving and saying what is neither acceptable nor rational.

"Thumma lā tunẓirūn" (then do not give me respite): that is, do not grant me delay.

"Ākhidhun bi-nāṣiyatihā" (I have hold of its forelock): that is, its Owner, its Subduer, and the One who disposes of it. It possesses no benefit or harm except by His permission.

"Inna rabbī ʿalā ṣirāṭin mustaqīm" (Indeed my Lord is upon a straight path): that is, upon the way of truth and justice.

"Fa-in tawallaw" (But if you turn away): its original form is tatawallaw, a present-tense verb from which one of the two tā' has been elided, and its meaning is "you turn your backs."

"ʿAlā kulli shay'in ḥafīẓ" (over everything a Guardian): that is, a watcher, and He will surely recompense every soul for what it has earned.

Meaning of the verses:

The context remains the story of Hud with his people, as God, exalted is He, reports the reply of the people of Hud to him. He says, "They said, 'O Hud, you have not brought us any clear proof'" (Qur'an 11:53), that is, an argument or evidence for the truth of what you call us to, namely the worship of God and the abandoning of the worship of our gods, and the acknowledgment of your prophethood. "And we will not abandon our gods on your word" (Qur'an 11:53), that is, their worship, "on your word" (Qur'an 11:53), that is, because of your saying that they do not deserve to be worshipped, since they neither benefit nor harm. "And we are not going to believe you" (Qur'an 11:53), that is, we will not follow you in your religion nor accept as true what you say. "We only say that some of our gods have struck you with evil" (Qur'an 11:54), that is, we find nothing to say about you except that some of our gods, which you revile and insult, have afflicted you with harm, with derangement and madness, so that you rave and babble and do not know what you are saying.

He replied to them, saying, "I call God to witness, and bear witness yourselves that I am free from what you associate" (Qur'an 11:54), so he openly declared his disavowal of their gods and that he does not fear them, refuting their claim that they had afflicted him with harm. He informed them that he calls God to witness to this, and then commanded them to bear witness likewise. His words "other than Him" (Qur'an 11:54) mean other than God, among all the other gods and associates. Then he challenged them, mocking them and their gods, saying, "So scheme against me, all of you, and give me no respite" (Qur'an 11:55), that is, plot to harm me, and do not delay or grant me time. Then he revealed to them the source of his strength, which is his reliance upon his Lord, saying, "Indeed I have relied upon God, my Lord and your Lord" (Qur'an 11:56), that is, I have entrusted my affair to Him and placed all my confidence in Him, so He will not hand me over to you nor forsake me among you. Then he informed them of the all-encompassing power of God over them and His dominion over them, saying, "There is no creature but that He holds its forelock" (Qur'an 11:56), that is, He subdues it and controls it, leading it wherever He wills and bringing upon it whatever punishment He wills. Then he informed them that his Lord, exalted is He, is upon the path of justice and truth, so He does not give His enemies power over His friends, saying, "Indeed my Lord is upon a straight path" (Qur'an 11:56), and therefore I am not fearful or apprehensive. Then he said to them, "But if you turn away" (Qur'an 11:57), that is, if you turn your backs on the truth and oppose it, that will not harm me, since I have conveyed to you what my Lord sent me with, and He will destroy you and bring in another people in your place, and you cannot harm Him in the slightest, neither little nor much. "Indeed my Lord is Guardian over all things" (Qur'an 11:57), that is, Watcher, and He will recompense each one for what he has earned, by His justice and mercy.

And to Him belong praise and grace.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Demonstration of the extent of the obstinacy and arrogance of the polytheists in every time and place.

2- The similarity of polytheistic thought and the condition of polytheists: the saying of the people of Hud, "We only say that some of our gods have struck you with evil," etc., is repeated by ignorant Muslims, who say, "So-and-so was struck by such-and-such a saint."

3- The stances of the people of faith are one: what Noah said to his people, challenging them, Hud also said to his people.

4- Affirmation of the principle that everything in the universe is subject to God's governance and does not go beyond what He wills for it or through it.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 11, verses 53–57:

Explanation of the words:

Bayyinah (clear proof): that is, with a proof and evidence for the truth of what you call us to, namely the worship of God alone.

"Wa ma nahnu bi-tarikī ālihatinā" (We will not abandon our gods): that is, abandoning the worship of our gods because of your saying that they do not deserve to be worshipped.

"Illā i'tarāka" (except that it has struck you): that is, it has afflicted you.

Bi-sū' (with harm): that is, with derangement, for you are raving and saying what is neither acceptable nor rational.

"Thumma lā tunẓirūn" (then do not give me respite): that is, do not grant me delay.

"Ākhidhun bi-nāṣiyatihā" (I have hold of its forelock): that is, its Owner, its Subduer, and the One who disposes of it. It possesses no benefit or harm except by His permission.

"Inna rabbī ʿalā ṣirāṭin mustaqīm" (Indeed my Lord is upon a straight path): that is, upon the way of truth and justice.

"Fa-in tawallaw" (But if you turn away): its original form is tatawallaw, a present-tense verb from which one of the two tā' has been elided, and its meaning is "you turn your backs."

"ʿAlā kulli shay'in ḥafīẓ" (over everything a Guardian): that is, a watcher, and He will surely recompense every soul for what it has earned.

Meaning of the verses:

The context remains the story of Hud with his people, as God, exalted is He, reports the reply of the people of Hud to him. He says, "They said, 'O Hud, you have not brought us any clear proof'" (Qur'an 11:53), that is, an argument or evidence for the truth of what you call us to, namely the worship of God and the abandoning of the worship of our gods, and the acknowledgment of your prophethood. "And we will not abandon our gods on your word" (Qur'an 11:53), that is, their worship, "on your word" (Qur'an 11:53), that is, because of your saying that they do not deserve to be worshipped, since they neither benefit nor harm. "And we are not going to believe you" (Qur'an 11:53), that is, we will not follow you in your religion nor accept as true what you say. "We only say that some of our gods have struck you with evil" (Qur'an 11:54), that is, we find nothing to say about you except that some of our gods, which you revile and insult, have afflicted you with harm, with derangement and madness, so that you rave and babble and do not know what you are saying.

He replied to them, saying, "I call God to witness, and bear witness yourselves that I am free from what you associate" (Qur'an 11:54), so he openly declared his disavowal of their gods and that he does not fear them, refuting their claim that they had afflicted him with harm. He informed them that he calls God to witness to this, and then commanded them to bear witness likewise. His words "other than Him" (Qur'an 11:54) mean other than God, among all the other gods and associates. Then he challenged them, mocking them and their gods, saying, "So scheme against me, all of you, and give me no respite" (Qur'an 11:55), that is, plot to harm me, and do not delay or grant me time. Then he revealed to them the source of his strength, which is his reliance upon his Lord, saying, "Indeed I have relied upon God, my Lord and your Lord" (Qur'an 11:56), that is, I have entrusted my affair to Him and placed all my confidence in Him, so He will not hand me over to you nor forsake me among you. Then he informed them of the all-encompassing power of God over them and His dominion over them, saying, "There is no creature but that He holds its forelock" (Qur'an 11:56), that is, He subdues it and controls it, leading it wherever He wills and bringing upon it whatever punishment He wills. Then he informed them that his Lord, exalted is He, is upon the path of justice and truth, so He does not give His enemies power over His friends, saying, "Indeed my Lord is upon a straight path" (Qur'an 11:56), and therefore I am not fearful or apprehensive. Then he said to them, "But if you turn away" (Qur'an 11:57), that is, if you turn your backs on the truth and oppose it, that will not harm me, since I have conveyed to you what my Lord sent me with, and He will destroy you and bring in another people in your place, and you cannot harm Him in the slightest, neither little nor much. "Indeed my Lord is Guardian over all things" (Qur'an 11:57), that is, Watcher, and He will recompense each one for what he has earned, by His justice and mercy.

And to Him belong praise and grace.
