2- The similarity of polytheistic thought and the condition of polytheists: the saying of the people of Hud, "We only say that some of our gods have struck you with evil," etc., is repeated by ignorant Muslims, who say, "So-and-so was struck by such-and-such a saint."

3- The stances of the people of faith are one: what Noah said to his people, challenging them, Hud also said to his people.

4- Affirmation of the principle that everything in the universe is subject to God's governance and does not go beyond what He wills for it or through it.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 11, verses 58–60:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And when Our command came⦆: that is, Our punishment, which was the violent wind (al-rih al-sarsar).

"By a mercy from Us": that is, by Our grace, favour and blessing.

"Obstinate tyrant" (jabbar 'anid): that is, one who is arrogant toward the truth, does not submit to it, and does not accept it.

"And on the Day of Resurrection": that is, and a curse on the Day of Resurrection.

"Ala, bu'dan li-'Ad" ("Oh, away with 'Ad!"): that is, destruction for 'Ad and their removal from every mercy.

The meaning of the verses:

The context still concerns Hud and his people. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And when Our command came⦆, that is, Our punishment, ﴿We saved Hud and those who believed with him by a mercy from Us﴾, that is, by kindness, favour and blessing, ﴿and We saved them from a severe punishment﴾, which is the punishment of the Day of Resurrection. Thus there were two salvations: a salvation in this world from the punishment of the barren, violent wind that destroyed everything by the command of its Lord, and a salvation from the punishment of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection, which is greater. And His saying, ﴿And that was 'Ad⦆, that is, these were 'Ad, the people of Hud, who denied the signs of their Lord, did not believe, and disobeyed His messengers, that is, Hud; the plural is used because whoever denies one messenger is considered to have denied all the messengers. ﴿And they followed the command of every obstinate tyrant⦆, that is, they followed the orders of the callers to misguidance, from among the arrogant people who opposed the truth, and so they led them to the wrath of Allah and His painful punishment. And His saying, ﴿And they were followed in this world by a curse⦆, that is, Allah sent after them His anger, wrath and destruction; and so it will be on the Day of Resurrection, and more severely. The account of this story is concluded with the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Verily, 'Ad disbelieved in their Lord⦆, that is, they denied Him and did not acknowledge His divinity and worship, ﴿Away with 'Ad!⦆, that is, destruction for 'Ad, the people of Hud. So let the polytheists of Quraysh take a lesson from this story, so that they may believe and affirm the Oneness of God, and thus be saved and prosper.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Affirmation of Tawhid (the Oneness of God), since the whole story is directed to this end.

2- Clarification of the sunnah (way) of Allah with earlier peoples: He sends messengers as bringers of good news and warners. If those addressed respond, they are made happy; if they do not respond, He gives them respite until the proof is established against them, then destroys them and saves the believers.

3- Condemnation of arrogance and obstinacy, for they are among the worst moral traits in a human being.

4- Following tyrants, oppression, disbelief and corruption leads only to ruin and loss.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 11, verses 61–63:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And to Thamud⦆ — i.e., We sent to the tribe of Thamud.

Their brother Salih — i.e., in lineage, for he was of the tribe of Thamud; between him and Thamud, the ancestor of the tribe, there were five forefathers.

And He made you settlers in it (wa-istamarakum) — i.e., He made you inhabitants of it, to populate it by dwelling and residing there.

Near, Responsive (qarib mujib) — i.e., near to His creation, since all worlds are before Him; and Responsive, i.e., to whoever calls upon Him.

You had hoped in him before this (marjuwwan qabla hadha) — i.e., before you said what you have said, we used to hope that you would be a leader among us.

Tell me (a-ra'aytum) — i.e., inform me.

Upon clear evidence from my Lord (ala bayyina min rabbi) — i.e., upon knowledge of my Lord, which He, glory be to Him, has taught me, so is it fitting for me to worship other than Him?

Not of loss (ghayra takhsir) — i.e., loss and destruction.

The meaning of the verses:

This is the beginning of the story of Salih with his people, for the Exalted said, informing of his being sent to his people: ﴿And to Thamud, their brother Salih⦆ — i.e., We sent to the tribe of Thamud, at al-Hijr between the Hijaz and al-Sham, their brother in lineage, not in religion, Salih. So he said: ﴿O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him⦆, addressing them by the title of kinship to unite their hearts to what he says to them. So he said: ﴿O my people, worship Allah⦆ — i.e., believe in Him and make Him one in worship, so do not worship anyone along with Him, for you have no god other than Him. He is your Lord, i.e., your Creator, your Provider, and the Manager of your affairs. ﴿He produced you from the earth⦆ — i.e., He began your creation by the creation of your father Adam from it; ﴿and made you settlers therein⦆ — i.e., He made you populate it by dwelling in it and living upon it. So seek His forgiveness by acknowledging His divinity, then turn to Him in repentance, worship Him alone, and do not associate anyone in His worship. His saying ﴿Indeed my Lord is near and responsive⦆ informs them of the nearness of the Lord, exalted is He, to His servants and His responsiveness to those who call upon Him, as an encouragement to them to faith and obedience and to abandoning polytheism and sins. This is what the first verse [61] contains. As for the second verse, it contains the people's reply to him, peace be upon him, for they said, as the Exalted related of them: ﴿O Salih, you were among us a man of hope before this⦆ — i.e., we used to hope for good from you and expected that you would be a leader among us, until you surprised us with what you call us to, namely abandoning our gods for your God. Then they denied his call, saying ﴿Do you forbid us to worship what our fathers worshipped?⦆ and informed him that they were not at ease regarding the soundness of what he calls them to of the monotheism of Allah, the Exalted, so they said ﴿And indeed we are in disquieting doubt about that to which you invite us⦆ — i.e., in doubt that produces unease, which is the agitation of the soul and its failure to settle upon what it has been told or informed of. This is what the second verse [62] contains. As for the third verse [63], it contains Salih's call to his people in an elevated manner, out of desire to establish proof against them, so that perhaps they would believe and make Allah one. He said, as Allah the Exalted informed in His saying: ﴿He said: O my people, tell me, if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord⦆ — i.e., upon certain knowledge of faith in my Lord and the obligation of worshipping and making Him one, and He has given me mercy from Himself, which is prophethood and messengership; so who will help me against Allah if I disobey Him? There is no one at all. Then, if I obeyed you in abandoning the worship of my Lord and consenting to the worship of your gods, you would add to me nothing but loss and misguidance, in this life and in the Hereafter.

Guidance of the verses:

1- The unity of means and end among all the messengers: the means is worship of Allah alone, and the end is the pleasure of Allah and Paradise.

2- The precedence of seeking forgiveness over repentance in the verse; its wisdom is that a person does not abandon his sin until he acknowledges it.

3- An explanation of a custom among people: the righteous man is hoped for among his family until, when he calls them to the truth and to abandoning falsehood, they dislike him, and they may openly tell him what the people of Salih told their prophet: ﴿You were among us a man of hope before this⦆.

4- The prohibition of responding to the people of falsehood in any form of response, for responding only increases the servant in loss.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 11, verses 69–73:

Explanation of the words:

*Bil-bushra* (with the good news): that is, with Isaac, and after Isaac, Jacob.

*Fa-ma labith* (then he did not delay): that is, he was not slow.

*Bi-ʿijlin ḥaneedh* (with a roasted calf): that is, roasted on stones.

*Lā taṣil ilayhi* (they did not reach it): that is, they did not touch it, so as to eat from it.

*Nakarahum* (he did not recognize them): that is, he did not know them.

*Awjasa* (he sensed fear): that is, he perceived fear and felt it.

*Lūṭ* (Lot): he is the son of Haran, the brother of Abraham, peace be upon him.

*Yā waylatā* (Oh, woe is me): that is, "Oh, woe is me! Come, this is the time of your coming."

*Wa hādhā baʿlī shaykhan* (and this, my husband, is an old man): a reference to Abraham, for he is her *baʿl*, that is, her husband.

*Inna hādhā la-shayʾun ʿajīb* (indeed, this is a wondrous thing): that is, a matter at which one marvels, finding it strange and improbable.

Meaning of the verses:

This is the good news given to Abraham, peace be upon him, with which God Most High gave him glad tidings, when He said, ﴿And certainly Our messengers came to Abraham with the good news﴾. The messengers meant here are Gabriel, Michael and Israfil, who entered upon him in his house and greeted him with peace; he returned the greeting, and this is the meaning of His words, ﴿They said, "Peace." He said, "Peace."﴾ His words, ﴿Then he did not delay to bring a roasted calf﴾, mean that he did not take long before bringing a roasted calf; *ḥaneedh* means *maḥnooth*, that is, roasted on stones. He brought it near to them and offered them the food by saying, ﴿Will you not eat?﴾ [al-Saffat: 91; al-Dhariyat: 27]. When he saw that their hands did not reach it, that is, they did not touch it, he did not recognize them (*nakarahum* meaning *ankarahum*), and he sensed fear of them, because it is customary that when a guest comes to someone and food is set before him and he does not eat, the host understands that he intends evil. When the angels saw this from him, they said to him, "Do not fear," and they explained the reason for their coming, saying, "We have been sent to the people of Lot," that is, to destroy and annihilate them because of their crimes. His wife was standing behind the curtain serving them along with Abraham. When she heard the news of the destruction of the people of Lot, she laughed with joy at the ruin of the people of wickedness. Then God Most High gave her good news through the angels of Isaac, and after him Jacob, that is, a child and a child's child. When she heard the good news, she struck her face in amazement, in the manner of women, and said, ﴿"Oh, woe is me! Shall I give birth while I am an old woman and this, my husband, is an old man"﴾, pointing to her husband Abraham, ﴿"shaykh"﴾, that is, of advanced age, for he was then a hundred years old and she was over ninety. ﴿"Indeed, this is a wondrous thing"﴾, that is, my giving birth at this age is a matter to be marvelled at. ﴿They said, "Do you wonder at the decree of God? The mercy of God and His blessings be upon you, O people of the house"﴾, that is, the house of Abraham. ﴿"Indeed, He is Praiseworthy and Glorious"﴾, that is, praised for His bounty and favour upon you; ﴿Glorious﴾ means possessing glory, praise and generosity. The wife of Abraham who was given the good news was Sarah, daughter of Abraham's paternal uncle, peace be upon him. The good news here is given to Abraham and his wife Sarah together, and it is twofold: the destruction of the wrongdoers, and Isaac and Jacob.

Guidance from the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- The recommendation of giving good news to a believer of what is good for him, even through a righteous dream.

2- The legislation of greeting someone who enters upon another, stands before him, or passes by him, and the obligation of returning the greeting.

3- The legislation of the household serving its guests, and the obligation of honouring the guest; in the authentic hadith: "Whoever believes in God and the Last Day, let him honour his guest."

4- The nobility of the household of Abraham, peace be upon him.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 11, verses 74–76:

Explanation of the words:

Al-Raw'(al-raw'): fright and fear.

Al-bushra (al-bushra): the good news that gladdens the heart.

Yujadiluna (yujadiluna): he argues with us, disputes with us.

Fi qawm Lut (fi qawm Lut): concerning the destruction of the people of Lut. Lut is the Messenger of Allah Lut ibn Haran, the nephew of Ibrahim.

Halim awwah (halim awwah): the halim is one who does not deal with punishment, and the awwah is one who often groans (utters "ah") at what displeases or saddens him.

A'ridh 'an hadha (a'ridh 'an hadha): leave off arguing about the people of Lut.

Ghayr mardud (ghayr mardud): no one can turn it back, because Allah the Exalted has decreed it, so it is certain to occur.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues to speak of the glad tidings given to Ibrahim. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿So when the fear had left Ibrahim and the good tidings had come to him, he began to argue with Us concerning the people of Lut.﴾ That is, the fear and dread of the angels left him before he recognised them, and the good tidings of a son and of the destruction of the people of Lut came to him. He began to dispute with the angels concerning the destruction of the people of Lut, because of the believers among them. He said: ﴿Indeed, in it is Lut.﴾ They answered him with their words that Allah the Exalted mentioned in Surat al-'Ankabut: ﴿We know best who is in it. We will surely save him and his family, except his wife; she is of those who remain behind.﴾ [Verse 32]. And the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, Ibrahim was forbearing, grieving, and turning back (to Allah)﴾ is the explanation for Ibrahim's argument with the angels concerning the people of Lut. Ibrahim had a tender heart, was forbearing, and did not deal with punishment; so he wished to delay the punishment from them in the hope that they would repent. He was awwah, humble and submissive, who often said "ah" when he saw or heard what displeased him; and munib, that is, repentant and returning to his Lord at all times. When Ibrahim persisted in arguing with the angels, they said to him: ﴿O Ibrahim, leave off this argument; indeed the command of your Lord has come,﴾ that is, the destruction of the people. ﴿And indeed there will come to them a punishment that cannot be turned back,﴾ that is, one that no one can repel, and this is what will be mentioned later in the context.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The permissibility of arguing on behalf of those from whom good is hoped, provided it is outside the prescribed legal limits (hudud) once they have been brought before the ruler.

2- The virtue of the character trait of forbearance (hilm).

3- The excellence of turning back to Allah the Exalted (inabah).

4- Allah's decree cannot be turned back: whatever Allah has judged will certainly occur.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 11, verses 77–80:

Explanation of the words:

Sa'a bihim (سيء بهم): i.e., he was distressed and worried by their coming to him.

Wa daqa bihim dharʿan (وضاق بهم ذرعا): i.e., his capacity was unable to bear the matter.

Yawmun ʿasib (يوم عصيب): i.e., severe and unbearable.

Yuhri'una ilayhi (يهرعون إليه): i.e., driven by the impulse of desire, they came hastening in disorder.

As-sayyiʾat (السيئات): i.e., the major sins, by mounting males.

Wa la tukhzuna fi dayfi (ولا تخزون في ضيفي): i.e., do not disgrace me or humiliate me by assailing my guests.

Rajulun rashid (رجل رشيد): i.e., a man of right judgment, reason, and knowledge of matters and their consequences.

Aw awi ila ruknin shadid (أو آوي إلى ركن شديد): i.e., to a strong clan that would protect me from you. He had no clan, because he was not from their homeland.

Meaning of the verses:

This is the opening of the account of Lut (peace be upon him) with the angels and then with his people. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And when Our messengers came to Lut﴾, and they were the guests of Ibrahim (peace be upon him), ﴿he was distressed on their account﴾, i.e., he was constricted and grieved, fearing for them from the criminals among his people. And he said, ﴿This is a severe day﴾, i.e., severe, because of what might happen in it of his guests being exposed to humiliation and disgrace while he was among them. This is what the first verse [77] indicates. As for the second [78], Allah the Exalted informs of the coming of Lut's people to him on that difficult day and critical hour. So the Mighty and Majestic says: ﴿And his people came to him, hastening toward him﴾, i.e., driven by the impulse of bestial desire, rushing. ﴿And previously they had been doing evil deeds﴾, i.e., before their coming they had been mounting men in their backsides. So he wanted to divert them from the guests, and said: ﴿O my people, these are my daughters; they are purer for you﴾, i.e., these are the women of the nation; they are purer for you, so marry them. ﴿And fear Allah﴾, i.e., fear His punishment, ﴿and do not disgrace me regarding my guests﴾, i.e., do not humiliate or degrade me concerning them. ﴿Is there not among you a man of right judgment?﴾ who enjoins what is good and forbids what is evil? They answered him, may Allah curse them, saying: ﴿You certainly know that we have no right to your daughters; and indeed you know what we want﴾, i.e., of committing the abomination with men. Here Lut (peace be upon him) said: ﴿If only I had against you some power﴾, i.e., supporters who would help me and aides who would assist me, I would have stood between you and what you desire, ﴿or I would take refuge in a strong support﴾, meaning a powerful clan he could shelter in, so it would protect him and his guests from his criminal people.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of the verses:

1- The virtue of honoring the guest and protecting him from everything that would harm him.

2- The abhorrence of evil customs and the change they bring about in a person.

3- Exerting every possible effort to repel evil, as Lut offered his daughters to protect his guests.

4- The worst kind of life is one in which there is no one who enjoins what is good and forbids what is evil.

5- Expressing the desire for strength to repel evil and avert what is hateful is praiseworthy.

**Explanation of the Words:**

**فأسر بأهلك** (*fa-asri bi-ahlika*): i.e., take your family out of the city by night.

**بقطع من الليل** (*biqt'in min al-layl*): i.e., during a portion and part of the night.

**الصبح** (*al-subh*): this is from the break of dawn (*fajr*) until sunrise.

**جعلنا عاليها** (*ja'alna 'aliyaha*): i.e., We made the upper part of the town its lower part.

**من سجيل** (*min sijjil*): i.e., of hardened clay.

**منضود** (*mandud*): i.e., arranged systematically, one above another.

**مسومة** (*musawwama*): i.e., marked with a special sign.

**عند ربك** (*'inda rabbika*): i.e., marked by the command of God, the Exalted.

**The Meaning of the Verses:**

The context continues to speak of the guests of Lut and his people. After Lut's distress intensified and he regretted his inability to protect the honored guests, saying, wishing, "If only I had strength against you, or could take refuge in a strong support," the angels said to him: ﴿O Lut, we are the messengers of your Lord﴾ sent to you; ﴿they will never reach you﴾ meaning, they will not reach you with any harm or even the slightest injury. ﴿So travel with your family by night, during a part of the night,﴾ meaning, by a portion and part of the night, ﴿and let none of you turn around,﴾ out of fear that they would see what descends upon the people of the punishment and be overcome with distress over it, ﴿except your wife; she will be struck by what strikes them.﴾ She was an old woman of evil, so leave her behind in the town. If she goes out, let her look back, for what strikes them will strike her as well.

Lut asked about the time the punishment would descend upon the people, and they said that their appointed time was the dawn. Lut had thought the time was delayed, so they said to him: ﴿Is not the dawn near?﴾

As for His saying, ﴿So when Our command came, We made its upper part its lower part﴾: meaning, when the command of God came to punish the people, He commanded Jibril (Gabriel), peace be upon him, who overturned it upon its inhabitants, so that the upper part of the town became its lower part, and the lower part its upper part. God rained upon them stones of hardened clay. Whoever was outside the town was struck by a stone and destroyed.

As for His saying, ﴿arranged in layers, marked﴾: meaning, some of them placed upon others, each stone bearing the name of the one it was to strike. As for His saying, ﴿marked by your Lord﴾: meaning, marked by the command of your Lord, O Messenger of God (ﷺ). ﴿And it is not far from the wrongdoers﴾: meaning, that destroyed town is not far from the wrongdoers, who are the polytheists of the Arabs. Or it may mean that the stones with which the people of Lut were destroyed are not far from the wrongdoers, i.e., their descent is not far from them.

**Guidance from the Verses:**

1. The recommendation of traveling by night, because of the blessing it contains in covering long distances without fatigue.
2. The reprehensibility of grieving excessively over the destruction of wrongdoers.
3. Signs of the power of God, Who overturned four cities within an hour, so that the upper became the lower and the lower became the upper.
4. A warning to wrongdoers in every time and place of the most severe and dreadful punishments.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 11, verses 84–86:

Explanation of the words:

"And to Madyan": that is, We sent to Madyan, to the people of Madyan.

"The measure and the scale": that is, when you sell to someone, do not diminish the measure and the scale.

"The punishment of an all-encompassing day": that is, it will encompass you from all your directions, so none of you will escape it.

"With justice": that is, with equity, meaning with fairness and evenness in buying and selling, on equal terms.

"And do not deprive": that is, do not diminish their rights, which are theirs upon you, in measuring and weighing and in other matters.

"And do not commit corruption on the earth": that is, do not spread corruption on the earth.

"What remains from Allah is better for you": that is, what remains for you after giving full measure and weight is better for you than the unlawful property that Allah has forbidden you.

"And I am not a guardian over you": that is, a watcher who observes your weighing and measuring. I am only a preacher and an adviser to you, nothing more.

The meaning of the verses:

This is the beginning of the account of Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, with his people, the people of Madyan. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And to Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb﴾, that is, We sent to the tribe of Madyan their brother in lineage, Shu'ayb. ﴿He said: O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him﴾, that is, affirm the oneness of Allah the Exalted; there is no god you may worship in truth except Him, since He is your Lord who created you, provided for you, and manages your affairs. His saying ﴿And do not diminish the measure and the scale﴾ means: do not diminish the measure when you measure for others, and the scale when you weigh for others. His saying ﴿Indeed, I see you in prosperity﴾ means: in ease and abundance of provision, ﴿and indeed, I fear for you the punishment of an all-encompassing day﴾ if you persist in polytheism, diminishing, and depriving, and it is a punishment that will encompass you so that none of you escapes. His saying ﴿And O my people, give full measure and weight with justice﴾ is a command to give full measure and weight with justice, after forbidding them from diminishing, to emphasize what he forbade them and to follow it with another prohibition, which is the prohibition of depriving people of their things, when he said ﴿And do not deprive people of their due﴾, that is, do not diminish their rights and what is rightfully theirs among all other rights. He forbade them from what is more general than that when he said ﴿And do not commit corruption on the earth, causing mischief﴾, that is, do not strive in the earth with corruption, and it includes all sins and prohibited acts. His saying ﴿What remains from Allah is better for you, if you are believers﴾ means: what remains for you after giving people their rights is better for you than what you take through diminishing and depriving, because of the blessing in the first and the loss in the second, if you are believers in the law of Allah and His promise and warning. His saying ﴿And I am not a guardian over you﴾ means: I am not a watcher over you when you buy and sell, nor a reckoner who counts your wrongdoing so that I may recompense you for it; I am only a preacher and an adviser to you, nothing more.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The unity of the message of the messengers, which begins with the affirmation of the oneness of Allah the Exalted, then commands and prohibitions to perfect and bring happiness to the human being after being saved from loss.

2- The prohibition of diminishing the measure and the scale is an especially grave prohibition.

3- The obligation to be content with the lawful, even if little, and to be displeased with the unlawful, even if abundant.

4- The prohibition of depriving people of their rights, such as the wages of workers, the prices of goods, and the like.

5- The prohibition of striving for corruption in the earth in any kind of corruption, the greatest of which is the abandonment of the laws of Allah the Exalted.

"And do not commit corruption on the earth": that is, do not spread corruption on the earth.

"What remains from Allah is better for you": that is, what remains for you after giving full measure and weight is better for you than the unlawful property that Allah has forbidden you.

"And I am not a guardian over you": that is, a watcher who observes your weighing and measuring. I am only a preacher and an adviser to you, nothing more.

The meaning of the verses:

This is the beginning of the account of Shu'ayb, peace be upon him, with his people, the people of Madyan. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And to Madyan [We sent] their brother Shu'ayb﴾, that is, We sent to the tribe of Madyan their brother in lineage, Shu'ayb. ﴿He said: O my people, worship Allah; you have no god other than Him﴾, that is, affirm the oneness of Allah the Exalted; there is no god you may worship in truth except Him, since He is your Lord who created you, provided for you, and manages your affairs. His saying ﴿And do not diminish the measure and the scale﴾ means: do not diminish the measure when you measure for others, and the scale when you weigh for others. His saying ﴿Indeed, I see you in prosperity﴾ means: in ease and abundance of provision, ﴿and indeed, I fear for you the punishment of an all-encompassing day﴾ if you persist in polytheism, diminishing, and depriving, and it is a punishment that will encompass you so that none of you escapes. His saying ﴿And O my people, give full measure and weight with justice﴾ is a command to give full measure and weight with justice, after forbidding them from diminishing, to emphasize what he forbade them and to follow it with another prohibition, which is the prohibition of depriving people of their things, when he said ﴿And do not deprive people of their due﴾, that is, do not diminish their rights and what is rightfully theirs among all other rights. He forbade them from what is more general than that when he said ﴿And do not commit corruption on the earth, causing mischief﴾, that is, do not strive in the earth with corruption, and it includes all sins and prohibited acts. His saying ﴿What remains from Allah is better for you, if you are believers﴾ means: what remains for you after giving people their rights is better for you than what you take through diminishing and depriving, because of the blessing in the first and the loss in the second, if you are believers in the law of Allah and His promise and warning. His saying ﴿And I am not a guardian over you﴾ means: I am not a watcher over you when you buy and sell, nor a reckoner who counts your wrongdoing so that I may recompense you for it; I am only a preacher and an adviser to you, nothing more.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The unity of the message of the messengers, which begins with the affirmation of the oneness of Allah the Exalted, then commands and prohibitions to perfect and bring happiness to the human being after being saved from loss.

2- The prohibition of diminishing the measure and the scale is an especially grave prohibition.

3- The obligation to be content with the lawful, even if little, and to be displeased with the unlawful, even if abundant.

4- The prohibition of depriving people of their rights, such as the wages of workers, the prices of goods, and the like.

5- The prohibition of striving for corruption in the earth in any kind of corruption, the greatest of which is the abandonment of the laws of Allah the Exalted.

**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 11, verses 87–90**

**Explanation of the words:**

**أصلاتك (Aṣalāتuka, "Does your prayer...?"):** That is, it is the excessive prayer you perform that has affected your mind, so that you now command us to do what is not fitting: to abandon the worship of our gods and to dispose of our wealth as we see fit.

**الحليم الرشيد (al-Ḥalīm al-Rashīd, "the forbearing, the rightly guided"):** That is, one possessed of forbearance (ḥilm) and right judgment (rushd). Ḥilm is the opposite of recklessness (ṭaysh), and rushd is the opposite of foolishness (safah). Their words were not a praise of him; rather, they were mockery of him.

**أن أخالفكم (An ukhālifakum, "that I should oppose you"):** That is, I do not wish to forbid you from something and then do it myself after you have left it.

**أن أريد إلا الإصلاح (In urīdu illā al-iṣlāḥ, "I desire only reform"):** That is, I desire nothing but reform for you.

**وما توفيقي إلا بالله (Wa mā tawfīqī illā billāh, "My success is only through God"):** That is, my success in the work of reform and in carrying it out comes only through God's favour upon me.

**وإليه أنيب (Wa ilayhi unīb, "and to Him I turn penitently"):** That is, I return to Him in all my affairs.

**لا يجرمنكم شقاقي (Lā yajrimannakum shiqāqī, "Let not my opposition bring you to..."):** That is, let not your opposition to me cause you to incur the punishment that befell the people of Noah and the nations after them.

**وما قوم لوط منكم ببعيد (Wa mā qawmu Lūṭin minkum bi-ba'īd, "The people of Lot are not far from you"):** That is, in time and in place, for the Lake of Lot is near the lands of Madyan, which lie between Ma'an and Jordan.

**رحيم ودود (Raḥīm Wadūd, "Merciful, Most Loving"):** That is, merciful to the believers, and loving to the God-fearing.

**Explanation of the verses:**

The noble context continues to speak of Shu'ayb (peace be upon him) and his people, the people of Madyan. When he commanded them to worship God alone and forbade them from diminishing the measure and the weight, from defrauding people of their goods, and from spreading corruption on the earth, for they used to clip the coins, circulate them, and rob the roads, they answered him with what God, exalted is He, reported of them in His words: ﴿They said, "O Shu'ayb, does your prayer command you that we leave what our fathers worshipped, or that we not do with our wealth what we wish?"﴾

By this speech they deny his forbidding them to worship the idols and images that their forefathers had worshipped, and they deny his forbidding them to diminish the measure and the scale and to defraud people of their goods, as well as his command to them to uphold truth and justice in these matters. They deny his forbidding and commanding them, and they attribute this to the excess of his prayers, which, in their view, had afflicted him with weakness of mind and lack of understanding. Their saying to him, ﴿Indeed, you are the forbearing, the rightly guided,﴾ was only sarcasm and mockery from them, not a belief in his forbearance and rectitude. Yet in reality he was, as they said, forbearing and rightly guided, for the forbearing is one whom anger does not drive to do what he would not do in a state of contentment, and the rightly guided is the opposite of the foolish, who does not handle wealth and other affairs well. This is what the first verse [87] contains.

As for the three verses that follow, they contain Shu'ayb's (peace be upon him) reply to their previous statement, when he said: ﴿O my people, tell me,﴾ that is, inform me, ﴿if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord,﴾ that is, upon proof and certain knowledge of His divinity, of what He loves and what He abhors, of His promise to His friends and His threat to His enemies, ﴿and He has provided me with good provision from Him,﴾ that is, lawful and good sustenance. Tell me, would it befit me to deny this truth and goodness and to go along with your falsehood? Certainly not. Another point: I do not desire to oppose you by doing what I forbid you from doing, for I do not command you to give full measure and weight while I myself diminish them, nor do I forbid you from worshipping idols while I worship them, nor do I forbid you from clipping coins while I clip them. Otherwise I would be like one who commands a thing and does not do it, or forbids a thing and does it, thereby deserving blame, reproach, the loss of trust, and disregard, so that his word is not heeded and his opinion is not acted upon.

Another matter: I do not desire, by what I command you or what I forbid you, anything but reform for you, to the extent that I am able and capable of it. My success in this comes only through God, my Lord and your Lord. In Him I place my trust in all my affairs, and to Him alone I turn penitently, that is, I submit in obedience and return in repentance. Then he called out to them, warning them against obstinacy and stubbornness, and said: ﴿And O my people, let not my opposition bring you to,﴾ that is, let not my opposition to you lead you to persist in disbelief and disobedience so that there befalls you a punishment like the punishment of the people of Noah, which was drowning, or the people of Hud, which was the destroying wind, or the people of Salih, which was the terrifying cry. ﴿And the people of Lot are not far from you,﴾ in time or in place, and you know what destruction and ruin befell them. That is, let not my opposition and enmity lead you to incur the punishment. Ask forgiveness of your Lord for what you are upon of polytheism and sins, then repent to Him through obedience. ﴿Indeed, my Lord is Merciful,﴾ who does not punish one who repents to Him, ﴿Most Loving,﴾ who loves one who turns to Him penitently.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. Indirect allusion close in meaning (ta'rīḍ, an oblique insult) carries the ruling of explicit slander (qadhf).
2. Disapproval of doing a thing after it has been forbidden, and of abandoning a thing after it has been commanded and urged.
3. Disapproval of obstinacy (lajāj) and stubbornness, for these prevent acknowledgement of the truth and commitment to it.
4. The obligation of seeking forgiveness and repenting from sins.
5. Describing the Lord, exalted is He, with mercy and love.

Explanation of the Words:

Musa (Moses): He is Musa ibn 'Imran, the one who spoke with Allah (Kalim Allah), and His messenger to the Children of Israel.

With Our signs: These are the nine signs, most of which are mentioned in the verse of al-A'raf.

And a clear authority: That is, with a strong proof against the enemy of Allah, Fir'awn (Pharaoh), so he defeated him by it.

And his chiefs: That is, the most noble men of Pharaoh's state.

And the command of Fir'awn was not right-guiding: That is, it was not guided, rather it was all foolishness.

He will lead his people: That is, he will go before them to the Fire, so he brings them down into it.

Wretched is the watering-place to which they are brought: That is, wretched and evil is the watering-place that leads to the Fire.

And they were followed in this by a curse: That is, a curse caught up with them in the life of this world, which was their drowning.

Wretched is the gift that is given: That is, wretched is the gift, which is the reward given to them, i.e., the one who gives it to them. What is meant is the curse of this world and the curse of the Hereafter.

Explanation of the Verses:

This is a brief glimpse of the story of Musa, peace be upon him, with Fir'awn, contained in four short verses. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And We sent Musa﴾, that is, after We sent Shu'ayb to the people of Madyan, We sent Musa ibn 'Imran, accompanied by Our signs that indicate Our sending him and the truth of what he calls to and demands, ﴿and a clear authority﴾, that is, a strong and manifest proof of the obligation of monotheism for Allah, the Exalted, and the falsehood of the divinity of anyone other than Him, like Fir'awn, upon whom be the curses of Allah. ﴿And Fir'awn said, "O chiefs, I know of no god for you other than me"﴾ [al-Qasas: 38]. His saying, the Exalted, ﴿to Fir'awn and his chiefs﴾: He was sent with Our signs and a clear authority to Fir'awn, the nobles of his soldiers, and the leaders of his state. Musa commanded them to follow the truth and abandon falsehood, but they refused and followed the command of Fir'awn, so he led them astray. ﴿And the command of Fir'awn was not right-guiding﴾, so that he would guide to success whoever follows him. Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿He will lead his people on the Day of Resurrection﴾, that is, he will go before them to the Fire and bring them down to its watering-places. ﴿And wretched is the watering-place to which they are brought﴾, that is, the Fire of Hell. His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And they were followed in this by a curse﴾, that is, Fir'awn and his people were cursed in this world, and on the Day of Resurrection they will also be cursed. ﴿Wretched is the gift that is given﴾, and these are the curse of this world and the curse of the Hereafter. The rifd is help and gift, and the marfud bihi is the one who is helped and given to those who are aided among people.

Guidance of the Verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Whoever Allah has decreed wretchedness for does not believe in the signs, but rejects them and denies them until he perishes.

2- The strength of proofs and the abundance of evidences do not necessitate people's submission and belief.

3- A warning against following the leaders of evil and the imams of corruption and misguidance.

4- Blame for the sources of falsehood, evil and corruption.

5- The worst of those punished is the one for whom the punishment of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter are combined.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 11, verses 100–102:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Dhalika⁠﴾ (that): a reference to the stories of the prophets that preceded in the surah.

﴿Min anba' al-qura⁠﴾ (some of the news of the towns): that is, the reports of the people of the towns: the people of Nuh, 'Ad, Thamud, the people of Lut, the companions of Madyan, and Pharaoh.

﴿Minha qa'imun wa hasid⁠﴾ (of them some still stand and some are mown down): some of them are cities whose traces remain, like the cities of Salih, and some of them are cities of which nothing remains, like the dwellings of 'Ad.

﴿Allati yad'una⁠﴾ (that they invoked): that is, they worshipped them through supplication and other forms of worship, such as slaughtering for them, making vows to them, and swearing by them.

﴿Ghayra tatbib⁠﴾ (other than ruin): that is, loss and destruction.

﴿Idha akhadh al-qura⁠﴾ (when He seizes the towns): that is, He punishes them for their sins.

﴿Alim⁠﴾ (painful): that is, severe, of very painful agony.

Meaning of the verses:

When Allah related to His Messenger in this surah what He related of the reports of earlier nations, He addressed him saying: ﴿That⁠﴾, that is, what has preceded in the narrative, ﴿is of the news of the towns⁠﴾, that is, of their people, which We relate to you, affirming your prophethood, establishing your message, strengthening your heart, and consoling you. His saying ﴿Of them some still stand and some are mown down⁠﴾ means: among those perished towns, some have traces standing, such as walls and ruins, and some are like the mown-down crop, with nothing standing or visible, because they have been obliterated and their traces have vanished. His saying ﴿And We did not wrong them⁠﴾ means: in destroying them, but they wronged themselves by associating partners with Allah, by sins, by denying Our signs, and by arrogance toward Our Messenger. His saying ﴿Then their gods, which they invoked besides Allah, did not avail them anything⁠﴾ means: their idols, which they took as gods and worshipped with various kinds of worship, such as supplication, vows, slaughter, and veneration, did not avail them in any way ﴿when the command of your Lord came⁠﴾ concerning their punishment, ﴿and they added nothing to them but ruin⁠﴾, that is, loss, destruction, and perdition. Then, in the last verse, Allah said to His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ: ﴿And such is the seizing of your Lord⁠﴾, that is, the seizing mentioned is the seizing of your Lord, ﴿when He seizes the towns⁠﴾, that is, the strongholds and cities with their inhabitants, while they are wrongdoers through associating partners with Allah and through sins. ﴿Indeed His seizing is painful, severe⁠﴾, that is, of intolerable and very severe agony. So will the polytheists, disbelievers, and wrongdoers today take heed, so that the polytheists abandon their polytheism, the disbelievers their disbelief, and the wrongdoers their wrongdoing, before Allah seizes them as He seized those before them?

Guidance of the verses:

1. Affirmation of the prophethood of Muhammad ﷺ, the spreading of his message, and consolation for him through what Allah relates to him of the news of earlier peoples.
2. Allah is exalted above injustice in destroying the people of polytheism and sin.
3. The gods of the polytheists did not avail them anything when retribution came upon them.
4. Condemnation of injustice and the evil end of wrongdoers.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 11, verses 103–109:

Explanation of the words:

*La-ayah* (لآية): that is, a sign that the One who punished in this world is able to punish in the Hereafter.

*Yawm mashhud* (يوم مشهود): that is, a day on which all creation witnesses it, and it is the Day of Resurrection.

*Illa li-ajal ma'dud* (إلا لأجل معدود): that is, the appointed term of the world, counted in days and hours.

*Illa bi-idhnihi* (إلا بإذنه): that is, except by the permission of Allah, the Exalted.

*Shaqiyy wa sa'id* (شقي وسعيد): that is, among the people of the place of standing there is one who is wretched from eternity and will enter the Fire, and among them is one who is happy from eternity and will enter the Garden.

*Zafir wa shahiq* (زفير وشهيق): that is, a intense sound, which is the *zafir*, and a weak sound, which is the *shahiq*.

*Ata' ghayr majdhudh* (عطاء غير مجذوذ): that is, not cut off, but lasting forever.

*Fa-la taku fi miryah mimma ya'budu ha'ula'* (فلا تك في مرية مما يعبد هؤلاء): that is, do not be in doubt about the falsity of the worship of these polytheists.

*Nasibahum ghayr manqus* (نصيبهم غير منقوص): what has been decreed for them of good or evil, mercy or punishment.

Meaning of the verses:

The words of the Exalted, ﴿Indeed, in that is a sign﴾, mean: indeed, in Allah's seizing of the wrongdoing nations and punishing them with the most severe kinds of punishment there is a sign, a clear indication that the One who punished in this world is able to punish in the Hereafter. Thus the believers in the meeting with Allah, the Exalted, find in what Allah has informed them of regarding the destruction of the wrongdoing nations a sign that serves as a lesson for them, so they persist in their piety toward Allah, the Exalted, until they meet Him while believing in Him and obeying His commands and prohibitions. And the words of the Exalted, ﴿That is a Day for which mankind will be gathered, and that is a Day witnessed﴾, mean: that in which the punishment of the Hereafter occurs is the Day of Resurrection, on which people will be gathered for the judgment to be decided, ﴿and that is a Day witnessed﴾, when all creation witnesses it. And the words of the Exalted, ﴿And We do not delay it except for a term numbered﴾, mean: the Day of Resurrection is delayed only for the completion of the lifespan of the world, counted in years, days, and even hours. And the words of the Exalted, ﴿On the Day it comes, no soul will speak except by His permission﴾, mean: by the permission of Allah, the Exalted. And His words, ﴿Among them is the wretched and the happy﴾, mean: people on that Day are divided between wretched and happy, and that returns to what was written for each person of wretchedness or happiness in the book of decrees, first, and to what they earned of good and evil, second. And the words of the Exalted, ﴿As for those who were wretched﴾, mean: by the judgment and decree of Allah, ﴿they will be in the Fire, for them therein will be groaning and wheezing﴾, where *zafir* is an intense sound and *shahiq* is a weak sound, and the two sounds accompany each other, as they are like the beginning and end of a donkey's bray. And the words of the Exalted, ﴿abiding therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure﴾, mean: for the duration of their existence. And His words, ﴿except what your Lord wills﴾, refer to those who will not be made to abide therein, namely the people of monotheism who died while committing major sins. And the words of the Exalted, ﴿Indeed, your Lord is an effector of what He intends﴾, mean: indeed your Lord, O human, is an effector of what He wills; when He wills something, He does it, and nothing can prevent Him from doing it. And His words, ﴿As for those who were made happy﴾, mean: Allah's judgment of their happiness, because Allah granted them success in faith, righteous deeds, and abandoning polytheism and sins, ﴿then in the Garden they will abide therein as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except what your Lord wills﴾, since the will of Allah is absolute and is limited only by His supreme will. And His words, ﴿a gift uninterrupted﴾, mean: a gift from your Lord to the people of His obedience that is never cut off, and this is the evidence of their eternal abiding therein.

And the words of the Exalted, ﴿So do not be in doubt concerning what these worship﴾, are an address to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, in which his Lord forbids him to doubt the falsity of the polytheists' worship of their idols, for they have no proof for the validity of their worship; they merely follow their forefathers, worshipping what they used to worship of idols and images. And the words of the Exalted, ﴿And indeed, We will give them their share without reduction﴾, inform that He will fully pay the polytheists what has been decreed for them of good and evil, or mercy and punishment, a complete payment in which there is no shortfall in any way.

Guidance from the verses:

1. The virtue and excellence of faith in the Hereafter.
2. The certainty of the final resurrection, and that there is no doubt about it.
3. Wretchedness and happiness were settled by the decree and destiny before the existence of the wretched and the happy.
4. The inability of every soul to speak on the Day of Resurrection until it is given permission to do so.
5. Allah's will is absolute: had He willed to bring out the people of the Fire, He would have brought them out, and had He willed to bring out the people of the Garden, He would have brought them out; but He judges by what He has informed of, and He is the Mighty, the Wise.

La-fi shakkin minhu murib: that is, placed in doubt (rayb), which is the agitation and unease of the soul.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 11, verses 114–115:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night﴾: i.e., perform the obligatory prayer.

"The two ends of the day": i.e., the dawn prayer, which is at the first end, and the noon (zuhr) and afternoon ('asr) prayers, which are at the second end.

"Approaches of the night" (zulafan min al-layl): i.e., hours of the night, and what is meant is the sunset (maghrib) prayer and the night ('isha') prayer.

﴿Indeed, good deeds erase bad deeds﴾: i.e., the good deeds of the five daily prayers erase the minor sins that occur between them.

﴿That is a reminder for those who remember﴾: i.e., that which was mentioned in His saying "And establish prayer" is an admonition for those who take heed.

"The doers of good" (al-muhsinin): i.e., those who make their intentions, words and deeds good by sincerity in them for Allah, and by performing them in the manner that Allah prescribed and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) explained.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues in directing the Messenger (ﷺ) and the believers and guiding them to what perfects them and brings them happiness. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and at the approach of the night﴾. Establish them in these five times: dawn, noon, afternoon, sunset and night. To establish them means to perform them in the most complete manner. That performance becomes good deeds by which Allah the Exalted erases bad deeds. His saying ﴿That﴾ refers to what is commanded and what follows from it, ﴿is a reminder﴾, i.e., an admonition, ﴿for those who remember﴾, i.e., those who take heed. And His saying ﴿And be patient﴾, i.e., in acts of obedience, both doing and abstaining, and in bearing the harm of the polytheists, and do not despair, ﴿for indeed, Allah does not allow the reward of the doers of good to be lost﴾, i.e., their recompense on the Day of Resurrection. The doers of good are those who sincerely dedicate their deeds to Allah the Exalted and perform them in the most complete manner, so that good deeds result for them, by which Allah erases bad deeds.

Guidance from the two verses:

1- Explanation of the times of the five prayers: the "two ends of the day" are the dawn, in which is the dawn prayer, and the evening (al-'ashiyy), in which are the noon and afternoon prayers; likewise "approaches of the night" are its hours, in which are the sunset and night prayers.

2- Explanation of Allah's custom that a good deed erases a bad deed. In the hadith: "The prayer from one prayer to the next is an expiation for what is between them, so long as major sins are not committed."

3- The obligation of patience and excellence (ihsan), and that they are among the best of deeds.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 11, verses 116–119:

Explanation of the words:

*Fa-lawla* (لولا): "lawla" is a word that expresses urging and exhortation to act.

*Min al-qurun* (من القرون): that is, the people of the generations; a qarn (generation) is one hundred years.

*Ulu baqiyyah* (أولو بقية): that is, people possessing a remnant, meaning of religion and virtue.

*Ma utrifu fihi* (ما أترفوا فيه): that is, what they were given in abundance of food, drink, clothing and enjoyments.

*Wa kanu mujrimin* (وكانوا مجرمين): that is, criminals against themselves by committing sins, and against others by driving them to that.

*Bi-zulm* (بظلم): that is, unjustly, without any sin they had committed.

*Ummah wahidah* (أمة واحدة): that is, one religion, which is Islam.

*Wa li-dhalika khalaqahum* (ولذلك خلقهم): that is, He created the people of discord for discord and the people of mercy for mercy.

The meaning of the verses:

The Exalted says to His Messenger, ﴿Why were there not among the generations before you, O Messenger, and the believers, people of a remnant﴾ of understanding, intellect, virtue and religion, ﴿who forbade corruption on the earth, except a few of those whom We saved﴾ — that is, why was there not such a group? It did not exist, except a few of those whom Allah saved when following the messengers at the destruction of their nations. His saying, ﴿And those who did wrong pursued what they had been given of luxury, and they were criminals﴾ — that is, there was not among them people of a remnant who forbade corruption on the earth, except a few whom Allah saved. All the others were wrongdoers to themselves through polytheism and sins, pursuing what they had been given of the enjoyments of worldly life, and thereby they were criminals. So Allah destroyed them and saved His messengers and the believers, as has been mentioned in the stories of Noah, Hud, Salih and Shu'ayb, peace be upon them. His saying, ﴿And your Lord would never destroy the towns unjustly while their people were reforming﴾ — that is, it is not the way of your Lord, O Messenger, to destroy the towns with injustice on His part while their people are righteous; rather, He destroys them because of their wronging themselves through polytheism, denial and sins. What this verse contains is an explanation of Allah's way in destroying the earlier nations whose accounts He related in this surah. His saying, ﴿And if your Lord had willed, He would have made mankind one community﴾ — that is, upon Islam, by placing guidance in their hearts and turning away the obstacles from them. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 11, verses 120–123:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Wa-kullan naqussu 'alayka min anba'i al-rusuli﴾: i.e., all that you need of the reports of the Messengers, We relate to you, to strengthen your heart.

﴿Ma nuthabbitu bihi fu'adak﴾: i.e., We relate to you of the stories that We use to make your heart firm, so that you may be patient in calling to Our religion and conveying it.

﴿Wa-ja'aka fi hadhihi al-haqq﴾: i.e., in this surah there has come to you the truth established from Allah, the Exalted, just as it came to you in other surahs.

﴿Wa-mawi'zatun wa-dhikra﴾: i.e., there has come to you in it an admonition and a reminder for the believers, since they are the ones who benefit from it.

﴿Wa-lillahi ghayb as-samawati wal-ard﴾: i.e., what is hidden of knowledge in them; Allah alone knows it, and no one else has knowledge of it.

﴿Fa-'budhu﴾: i.e., affirm His oneness in worship and do not associate anything with Him.

﴿Wa-tawakkal 'alayhi﴾: i.e., entrust your affair to Him and place complete trust in Him, for He is sufficient for you.

Meaning of the verses:

When Allah, the Exalted, related to His Messenger in this noble surah the reports of the Messengers with their peoples, showing what the Messengers encountered from individuals of their peoples of denial, obstinacy and rejection, and how the Messengers were patient until victory came to them, Allah, the Exalted, informed His Messenger, saying: ﴿And all that We relate to you of the news of the Messengers is that by which We make firm your heart﴾. That is: and We relate to you everything you need in strengthening your position and the firmness of your resolve, from the reports of the Messengers, i.e., their accounts with their peoples, that by which We make your heart firm so that you continue your call and convey your message. His saying ﴿And there has come to you in this﴾: i.e., in this surah, the truth of the reports as it came to you in other [surahs]. ﴿And an admonition﴾ for you by which you admonish others, ﴿and a reminder﴾ by which the believers are reminded, so they remain firm upon the truth and are patient in obedience and in trials, neither despairing nor growing weary. His saying: ﴿Say to those who do not believe: "Work according to your position; indeed we are working. And wait; indeed we are waiting"﴾. That is: say, O Our Messenger, to those among your people who do not believe, who are persistent in denial, polytheism and disobedience: "Act upon your state and what you are established in; indeed we are acting upon our state likewise."

﴿And wait; indeed we are waiting﴾ to see which of us will be victorious in the end or which will be defeated. His saying: ﴿And to Allah belongs the unseen of the heavens and the earth﴾: He alone knows when victory will come and when defeat will be decreed. And to Him the whole matter returns: the matter of victory and defeat, just as the matter of guidance and misguidance, and of happiness and wretchedness. Therefore, ﴿so worship Him﴾, O Our Messenger, alone, and ﴿rely upon Him﴾ alone, for He is sufficient for you in all that concerns you of this world and the Hereafter. ﴿And your Lord is not unaware of what you do﴾, O people, and He will recompense each with what he has done of good or evil, and He is over all things competent.

Guidance of the verses:

From the guidance of these verses:

1- Explanation of the benefit of the Qur'anic narratives, which include:
a) Strengthening the heart of the Prophet ﷺ.
b) Providing admonitions and lessons for the believers.
c) Establishing the prophethood of the Messenger ﷺ.

2- Knowledge of the unseen belongs to Allah alone; no one else knows it.

3- The return of all matters is to Allah: in beginning, in return, and in end.

4- The obligation of worshipping Allah, the Exalted, and relying upon Him.
